The map after 1458 is therefore assembled with tools/riken.py: the small states plus the large states in Cliopatria, among others the Habsburgs' lands, Bohemia, Brandenburg and Prussia, Saxony (also under the union with Poland in 1697–1763), Bavaria, Hanover, Lorraine, Savoy, Milan and Florence, the lands of Spain and Denmark in the empire and the German territories that Sweden held from 1632. Only the part of them that lies inside the empire's border in 1458 in Cliopatria is counted, without Hungary and Prussia. Areas that an empire outside takes over, for example France's conquests in the west, drop out of the map, also when they were only occupied for a short time. Switzerland and the United Netherlands are shown up to and including 1647. The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 made Switzerland formally independent of the empire. For the Netherlands the sources differ: they left the empire in practice in 1581, Spain recognised the republic in 1648 and the emperor accepted its neutrality in 1653 (the Imperial Diet in 1728). The map removes them from 1648. The Burgundian Netherlands (roughly present-day Belgium) lay for the most part outside Cliopatria's border in 1458 and are therefore not visible, although they belonged to the empire. The area after 1458 is calculated from the assembled map: about 0.8 million km² in 1460–1600 and about 0.7 million km² in 1648–1790. Wikipedia gives, after the historian Peter Wilson, about 690,000 km² for the empire's German- and Czech-speaking parts in 1648–1792, without the Italian- and French-speaking parts.

summary.en: The Tang dynasty ruled China in 618–907, with an interruption in 690–705. It is often regarded as a high point in Chinese history, with a cosmopolitan culture and the greatest flowering of Chinese poetry.

text.en: The Li family founded the dynasty in 618, when the Sui dynasty collapsed. The early emperors' campaigns gave a larger empire than the Han Empire's.

An Lushan's rebellion (755–763) devastated the country and weakened central power. In the 9th century regional military governors (jiedushi) gained ever more power, and peasant revolts led to great population losses. In 907 Zhu deposed the last emperor, Ai, and took the throne himself. The Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period then followed.
Chang'an, present-day Xi'an (618–690 and 705–904), and Luoyang (904–907). For much of the period Chang'an was the world's most populous city.

Emperor Gaozu (618–626), Emperor Taizong (626–649), Emperor Xuanzong (712–756) and the last, Emperor Ai (904–907). Wu Zetian took the throne in 690 and proclaimed a dynasty of her own, Wu Zhou; she is the only recognised female emperor in Chinese history.
About 5.4 million km² in 715, according to Wikipedia's fact box. The map data (Cliopatria) gives at most about 8.7 million km² in 661–665. The sources thus differ greatly.

Censuses in the 7th and 8th centuries gave about 50 million inhabitants, and towards the end the population is estimated at 80 million. Officials were recruited through state examinations. The poets Li Bai and Du Fu lived under the Tang, and woodblock printing developed. Buddhism gained great influence but was pushed back by Emperor Wuzong in the 840s.
The Li family takes power when the Sui dynasty falls, and Gaozu becomes the first emperor.

mapNote.en: The map data begins in 623.

text.en: The general Su Dingfang defeats the khagan of the Western Turks, and the Western Turkic Khaganate is annexed. Emperor Gaozong sets up protectorates that extend China's influence all the way to Herat in present-day Afghanistan.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire growing in steps from 633 and being at its largest in 661–665.

text.en: Wu Zetian takes the throne and proclaims the Wu Zhou dynasty. The Tang dynasty is restored in 705.

mapNote.en: The map data shows no interruption in 690–705.

text.en: The general An Lushan rebels, and the war lasts until 763. It destroys the Tang's prosperity. The Tibetans take advantage of the situation, and after 763 the Tang cannot take back Central Asia.

mapNote.en: The map shows the decrease from 757.

text.en: Zhu deposes Emperor Ai and takes the throne. The Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms follow.

mapNote.en: The map data ends in 910.
The sources give 618–907. The map data (Cliopatria) runs 623–910 and shows no interruption for Wu Zhou in 690–705.

summary.en: The Song dynasty ruled China in 960–1279. It is divided into the Northern Song, with its capital at Kaifeng, and the Southern Song, with its capital at Hangzhou. The period is known for its economy and its inventions, among them the first banknotes, gunpowder weapons and the compass.

text.en: The general Zhao Kuangyin, Emperor Taizu, took the throne from the Later Zhou in 960 and then conquered the rest of the Ten Kingdoms.

The Jurchen people's Jin dynasty took northern China in 1127, and the court fled south of the Yangtze. The Mongols conquered the Jin in 1234. Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty in 1271, and after two decades of war the Southern Song was defeated at Yamen in 1279.

Bianjing, present-day Kaifeng (960–1127), and under the Southern Song Lin'an, present-day Hangzhou. In between the court was, among other places, at Yingtian and Yangzhou; WHE states that Hangzhou became the capital in 1138.
Emperor Taizu (960–976), who founded the Northern Song, Emperor Gaozong (1127–1162), who founded the Southern Song, and the last, Zhao Bing (1278–1279).

According to Wikipedia's fact box about 3.1 million km² in 980, 2.1 million in 1127 and 1.8 million in 1204. The map data (Cliopatria) gives about 2.8 million km² for the Northern Song and 2.1 million for the Southern Song.

The Northern Song is estimated to have had about 90 million inhabitants. The Song was the first in the world with real banknotes and the first Chinese state with a standing navy. The oldest surviving recipes for gunpowder date from this time, and the compass was used to find north. Printing spread, and movable type was invented in the 11th century.
The army proclaims the general Zhao Kuangyin emperor. He founds the Song dynasty and then conquers the Ten Kingdoms.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire growing in 970 and 980.

text.en: The Jurchens take the capital and capture the former emperor Huizong, Emperor Qinzong and most of the court. The court flees south, and the Southern Song begins.

mapNote.en: The map data switches to the Southern Song only in 1139. WHE gives 1125 as the border between the Northern and Southern Song.

text.en: The Mongols have conquered the Jin and taken northern China in 1234. The year after, their attack on the Song begins.

mapNote.en: The map shows decreases from 1241.

text.en: The Mongols take the capital Lin'an.
Kublai Khan's army defeats the Southern Song at Yamen. China is united under the Yuan dynasty.

mapNote.en: The map data ends in 1278.
The sources give 960–1279. The map data (Cliopatria) runs 961–1278 and switches from the Northern to the Southern Song in 1139. Wikipedia gives 1127 and WHE 1125 for the switch; the sources differ.

summary.en: The Khmer Empire was an empire in Southeast Asia centred in present-day northern Cambodia. The period is called the Angkor era after the best-known capital, Angkor, with the temples Angkor Wat and Bayon.

text.en: The empire emerged from the earlier Chenla culture. The start is counted from 802, when the prince Jayavarman II proclaimed himself universal ruler (chakravartin) in the Phnom Kulen mountains.

The end is traditionally counted from 1431, when Angkor fell to the Siamese kingdom of Ayutthaya and the king left the city for the area around Phnom Penh. Why the empire fell is disputed. Scholars point, among other things, to heavy monsoon rains followed by severe drought, which damaged the water systems.
Mahendraparvata (early 9th century), Hariharalaya (middle of the 9th century), Yasodharapura, that is Angkor (late 9th century–928 and 944–1431), and Lingapura, present-day Koh Ker (928–944).

Jayavarman II (from 802), Suryavarman II (1113–1150), who had Angkor Wat built, and Jayavarman VII (from 1181), who is regarded as the empire's greatest king. The sources give different years for his death: 1218 or 1219 in Wikipedia and 1215 in WHE.

About 1 million km² in 1290, according to Wikipedia's fact box. The empire comprised large parts of present-day Cambodia, Thailand, Laos and southern Vietnam. The map data (Cliopatria) gives at most about 950,000 km² in 1206–1219.

Language: Old Khmer, and Sanskrit in religion. Religion: Hinduism and Buddhism. Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century and was originally dedicated to Vishnu. Satellite images show that Angkor with its water system was the world's largest pre-industrial urban complex in the 11th–13th centuries.
Jayavarman II proclaims himself universal ruler in the Phnom Kulen mountains. This is counted as the beginning of the Khmer Empire.

mapNote.en: The map data shows only a small area in 800–805 and the empire from 806.

text.en: Under Suryavarman II the temple Angkor Wat is built; WHE states that construction began in 1122. His campaigns against Champa and Dai Viet fail, but in 1145 he sacks Champa's capital Vijaya.
A fleet from Champa sacks Angkor, and the Khmer king is killed.
Jayavarman VII takes back Angkor and becomes king in 1181. After 22 years of war the Khmers defeat Champa in 1203 and conquer large parts of the country. He has the Bayon built as the state temple.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire growing in 1188 and being at its largest in 1206–1219.

text.en: Under pressure from Dai Viet and its ally Champa, the Khmers withdraw from many of the conquered provinces.

mapNote.en: The map shows the decrease in 1220.

text.en: Ayutthaya takes Angkor, and King Ponhea Yat moves to the area around Phnom Penh. This is counted as the end of the Khmer Empire.

mapNote.en: The map data continues with the smaller Khmer empire until 1867.
The sources give 802–1431. The map data (Cliopatria) runs 800–1867 and includes the smaller Cambodian kingdom after the fall of Angkor.

summary.en: The Ghana Empire, also called Wagadu, was an empire in the western Sahel, in present-day south-eastern Mauritania and western Mali. It grew rich on the trade in gold to the north and salt to the south. It has no geographical connection with present-day Ghana, which took the name in 1957.

text.en: It is uncertain when the empire arose. Wikipedia gives about the year 300 and WHE at least the 6th century. The first known written record of the royal dynasty comes from al-Khwarizmi in the year 830.

The empire declined from the 12th century and in the 13th century became a vassal of the Mali Empire; Mali's king Sundiata took the old capital in 1240, according to WHE. According to an old view the empire was conquered by the Almoravids in 1076–1077. WHE writes that the capital was sacked by the Almoravids around 1076, while Wikipedia writes that modern scholars strongly question that any conquest took place. The sources differ.
Probably Koumbi Saleh, according to Wikipedia possibly a later capital. The historian Dierk Lange holds that the empire's core instead lay at Lake Faguibine in the Niger Bend.
The names of the early kings are unknown. Tunka Manin corresponded with the Almoravids in the 11th century. The kings were also called kaya maghan, king of gold.
About 650,000 km² in 1000, according to Wikipedia's fact box. The map data (Cliopatria) shows an unchanged area of about 200,000 km² throughout.

Languages: Soninke, Malinke and other Mande languages. Religion: traditional African religion, later Islam (from the 11th century). The empire profited from a monopoly on the gold that went north and the salt that went south. According to Wikipedia the empire did not itself rule the goldfields, while WHE mentions gold from the Bambuk fields among the empire's own assets.
Al-Khwarizmi mentions Ghana's royal dynasty. It is the first known written record of it.

mapNote.en: The map data begins in 793.

text.en: The Almoravids take Awdaghost, which was then one of the king's seats.
According to WHE the Almoravids sack the capital Koumbi Saleh around 1076. Wikipedia writes that the story of an Almoravid conquest in 1076–1077 is strongly questioned by modern scholars.
Sundiata Keita, the founder of the Mali Empire, takes the old capital. Ghana becomes part of Mali's sphere of power.

mapNote.en: The map data ends in 1201.
Wikipedia gives about the year 300 to the middle of the 13th century, WHE at least the 6th century to the 13th century. The map data (Cliopatria) runs 793–1201 with the same border throughout.

summary.en: The Mali Empire was an empire in West Africa, founded by Sundiata Keita around 1235. It became known for its rich kings, especially Mansa Musa, and at its height was the largest empire in West Africa.

text.en: The empire began as a small Mandinka kingdom on the upper course of the Niger River, in the Manding area. Sundiata Keita defeated the Sosso Empire at the Battle of Kirina around 1235, and Mali became a great power.

After King Suleyman's death, after 19 years on the throne from 1341, a slow decline began. According to WHE the Songhai conquered most of the empire around 1468. According to Wikipedia Mali was still large in the 15th century and lost land to the Songhai and other neighbours from 1507. After a severe defeat at Djenné in 1599 the empire fell apart, and the Keita family withdrew to Kangaba.
Disputed. WHE gives Niani, a city that no longer exists, probably near the Sankarani River. According to Wikipedia the location is contested.
Sundiata Keita (about 1235–1255; WHE gives 1230–1255), Mansa Musa (about 1312–1337) and Suleyman (from 1341).
About 1.3 million km² in 1350, according to Wikipedia's fact box. The map data (Cliopatria) gives at most about 1.1 million km² in 1415–1462.

Language: Manding. Religion: traditional African religion and Islam. Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324–1326 became famous: his gifts and his gold caused inflation in Egypt. Timbuktu became a famous centre of learning, and Ibn Battuta visited Mali in Suleyman's time.
Sundiata Keita defeats the Sosso Empire at Kirina. Mali becomes a great power, and in 1240 Sundiata takes the Ghana Empire's old capital.

mapNote.en: The map data begins in 1236.

text.en: Mansa Musa travels to Mecca via Cairo. His gifts and spending in gold make gold fall in value in Egypt.

According to WHE the Songhai king Sunni Ali conquers most of the Mali Empire around 1468. According to Wikipedia Mali loses land to the Songhai and other neighbours only from 1507. The sources differ.

mapNote.en: The map shows decreases in 1463 and 1468 and the largest in 1475.

text.en: Mali tries to take advantage of the Songhai's fall after the Moroccan invasion of 1593, but a severe defeat outside Djenné in 1599 ends the attempt. The empire falls apart into independent chiefdoms.

mapNote.en: The map data ends in 1611.
Wikipedia gives about 1235–1610, WHE 1240–1645. The map data (Cliopatria) runs 1236–1611.

summary.en: Kievan Rus' was the first East Slavic state, later a confederation of principalities, in Eastern Europe from the late 9th century to the middle of the 13th century. It was ruled by the Rurik dynasty. Belarus, Russia and Ukraine all count Kievan Rus' as their cultural origin.

text.en: According to the Primary Chronicle the Varangian prince Oleg was the first to unite the East Slavic lands. He set out from Novgorod, took control along the Dnieper and took Kiev, according to Wikipedia around 882. WHE counts the empire from 862, when Rurik founded the dynasty.

The empire began to decline in the late 11th century and in the 12th century fell apart into rival principalities. Trade decreased as Byzantium weakened. The Mongol invasion of 1237–1241 and the siege of Kiev in 1240 ended the empire. WHE gives 1242 as the end year.
Oleg the Wise (about 882–912), Sviatoslav I (943–972), Vladimir the Great (980–1015) and Yaroslav the Wise (1019–1054).

The empire was at its largest in the middle of the 11th century, under Yaroslav the Wise, and stretched from the White Sea to the Black Sea and from the Carpathians to the Taman Peninsula. Wikipedia's fact box gives about 1.33 million km² and 5.4 million inhabitants in 1000. The map data (Cliopatria) gives at most about 1.2 million km² in 1034–1235.

Languages: Old East Slavic, Church Slavonic (written language), Old Norse and Finnic languages. Religion: Slavic paganism and then Orthodox Christianity. Yaroslav's sons issued the first written law, the Russkaya Pravda, soon after his death.

The trident is found on the gold and silver coins that Grand Prince Vladimir minted (980–1015) and was used by his sons, as an emblem of the Rurikid house. Similar emblems are found on Sviatoslav I's seal. It is thus attested for part of the empire's time. Scholars disagree about where the emblem came from; according to Omeljan Pritsak it has a Khazar origin.
Oleg the Wise moves south from Novgorod along the Dnieper and takes Kiev, which becomes the empire's capital.

mapNote.en: The map data begins in 882.

text.en: Sviatoslav I makes the first great conquest and defeats the Khazar Khaganate in the east.

mapNote.en: The map shows an increase in 970–979.

text.en: Vladimir the Great is baptised and introduces Christianity in Kiev and the rest of the empire.
Under Yaroslav the Wise the empire reaches its greatest extent. His sons issue the law code Russkaya Pravda in the 1050s.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire at its largest from 1034.

text.en: The Mongol invasion of 1237–1241 reaches Kiev, which falls after a siege in 1240.

mapNote.en: The map data shows only a very small area in 1236–1240.
Wikipedia gives about 880–1240, WHE 862–1242. The map data (Cliopatria) runs 882–1240, with almost no area in the last years 1236–1240.

summary.en: The Timurid Empire was a Turco-Mongol, Persianate Muslim empire that dominated Greater Iran in the early 15th century. It was founded by Timur (Tamerlane) and comprised present-day Iran, Iraq and Afghanistan, large parts of Central Asia and parts of the Caucasus, Pakistan, northern India and Turkey.

text.en: Timur came from the Barlas tribe, of Mongol origin but Turkicised in Central Asia. He began his conquests in 1363 and founded the empire in 1370. He saw himself as the heir of Genghis Khan's Mongol Empire.

Timur died in 1405 on the way to Mingkina. His descendants lost most of Persia to the Aq Qoyunlu, when Abu Sa'id Mirza was defeated and died in 1469. By 1507 the Uzbeks under Shaybani Khan had taken almost all the remaining Timurid principalities, including Samarkand and Herat. The Timurid prince Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India in 1526.
Timur (1370–1405), Shah Rukh (1405–1447), his son the astronomer and mathematician Ulugh Beg (1447–1449), Husayn Bayqara (1469–1506) and the last, Badi al-Zaman (1506–1507).
About 4.4 million km² in 1405, according to an estimate in Wikipedia's fact box. The map data (Cliopatria) gives at most about 5.1 million km² in 1402–1406.

Language: Persian (official, court and administration), Chagatai Turkic and Arabic. Religion: Sunni Islam. Under Shah Rukh and Ulugh Beg the Timurid Renaissance flourished. Timur forcibly moved scholars, artists and craftsmen to Samarkand, which became a great cultural city.

Three rings in a triangle, Timur's emblem. The Castilian envoy Ruy de Clavijo, who visited Timur in 1403, and the historian Ibn Arabshah described it on Timur's seals and coins. According to Clavijo the rings stood for the three parts of the world that Timur was lord of, but what the emblem meant is not known for certain.
Timur takes sole power in Transoxiana and makes Samarkand the capital.

mapNote.en: The map data begins in 1375.

text.en: Timur begins his campaigns to the west in 1380. He takes Isfahan in 1387, defeats the Muzaffarids at Shiraz in 1393 and drives the Jalayirids out of Baghdad.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire growing in steps in 1385, 1395 and 1402.

text.en: Timur invades the Delhi Sultanate, defeats the sultan's army and sacks Delhi.
After sacking Baghdad in 1401, Timur defeats the Ottomans under Sultan Bayezid I at Ankara.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire at its largest in 1402–1406.

text.en: Timur dies on the way to Mingkina. Shah Rukh then rules from Herat, and under him and Ulugh Beg the Timurid Renaissance flourishes.

mapNote.en: The map shows a decrease from 1407.

text.en: The Uzbeks under Shaybani Khan have taken almost all the Timurid principalities, including Samarkand and Herat. The Timurid prince Babur continues from Kabul and founds the Mughal Empire in India in 1526.

mapNote.en: The map data continues to 1528 with Timurid territories around Kabul.
Wikipedia gives 1370–1507. The map data (Cliopatria) runs 1375–1528 and includes the Timurid territories around Kabul after 1507.

summary.en: The Aztec Empire was a confederation, a triple alliance, of three Nahuatl-speaking city-states in the Valley of Mexico: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan. It ruled large parts of central Mexico until the Spaniards and their Indigenous allies defeated it in 1521.

text.en: The Mexica founded the city of Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco in 1325. The alliance was formed in 1428, after a civil war against the city of Azcapotzalco and the Tepanecs. World History Encyclopedia counts the Aztec Empire from about 1345, Wikipedia from 1428.

Hernán Cortés came in 1519 and made alliances with, among others, Tlaxcala and the Totonacs, who wanted to be free of the Aztecs. A smallpox epidemic killed more than half the population in the area. Tenochtitlan fell in 1521 to the Spaniards and an army of Tlaxcalans, Texcocans, Totonacs and others.
Tenochtitlan, which with time became the alliance's real centre.

Itzcoatl (1427–1440) founded the alliance. Ahuitzotl (1486–1502) conquered the Oaxaca Valley and the Soconusco coast. Moctezuma II (1502–1520) ruled when the Spaniards came, and Cuauhtémoc was the last ruler.
About 220,000 km² in 1520, most of central Mexico and some more distant provinces in Mesoamerica.
Classical Nahuatl was the common language. Conquered peoples were allowed to keep their own gods as long as they also worshipped the empire's god of war.
The Aztecs ruled indirectly: conquered cities kept their rulers if they paid tribute twice a year and provided soldiers.

The eagle on the cactus is Tenochtitlan's emblem, and that is how the capital appears in the Codex Mendoza. According to the story of the city's founding the Mexica settled on an island in Lake Texcoco where an eagle had its nest on a cactus, and they interpreted it as a sign from their gods. In the sources the eagle sometimes eats a snake, sometimes something else, and in the Codex Mendoza it stands alone.
The Mexica found their city on an island in Lake Texcoco.

mapNote.en: The map shows the city of Tenochtitlan from 1326.

text.en: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan win the war against the Tepanecs and form the alliance. It immediately begins to conquer areas outside the Valley of Mexico.

mapNote.en: The map shows the alliance from 1429.

text.en: Ahuitzotl puts down revolts and then conquers the Oaxaca Valley and the Soconusco coast near present-day Guatemala.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire at its largest from 1502.

text.en: Cortés lands on the coast and receives help from Totonacs and Tlaxcalans, who were enemies of the Aztecs.
After a smallpox epidemic and a long siege the capital falls, and Cuauhtémoc is taken prisoner.

mapNote.en: The map shows the alliance up to and including 1520.

The sources differ: Wikipedia gives 1428–1521 for the alliance, World History Encyclopedia about 1345–1521 for the Aztec Empire. The map shows the city of Tenochtitlan in 1326–1428 and the alliance in 1429–1520.

summary.en: The Inca Empire, Tawantinsuyu, was the largest empire in the Americas before Columbus. From Cusco in the Andes the Incas ruled an area from present-day Ecuador to Chile, until the Spaniards conquered it in the 1530s.

text.en: The Incas lived in the Cusco Valley in the Peruvian highlands. Around 1438 Pachacuti defeated the Chanca people, and then the empire began to grow in all directions.

After a civil war between the brothers Huáscar and Atahualpa (1529–1532) the Spaniards under Francisco Pizarro began to conquer the empire in 1532. Diseases such as smallpox may have spread in the empire even before the Spaniards came. Manco Inca continued the resistance from Vilcabamba, which fell in 1572.
Cusco.
Pachacuti (1438–1471), Topa Inca Yupanqui (1471–1493), Huayna Capac (1493–1525), Huáscar and Atahualpa.
About 2 million km² in 1527, from Quito in the north to Santiago in the south. The empire had about 10 million inhabitants who spoke over 30 languages.
Quechua was the official language, but many other languages were spoken. The Incas promoted the worship of the sun god Inti, and many local sacred places (huacas) continued to be worshipped.
The Incas built an enormous road network and kept count with knotted cords, khipu, but had neither writing, the wheel nor iron. Taxes were paid with labour instead of money.

The mascapaicha, the royal headband with a red fringe and feathers, was the empire's imperial symbol. Only the Sapa Inca, the king in Cusco and emperor of Tawantinsuyu, was allowed to wear it, and it was the visible sign of the highest power in the empire.
Pachacuti defeats the Chanca, and the Incas begin to build an empire in the Andes.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire from 1440.

title.en: The empire reaches its greatest size

text.en: Topa Inca Yupanqui and Huayna Capac extend the empire along the Andes to the north and south.

mapNote.en: The map shows a large increase from 1497.

text.en: Pizarro takes Atahualpa prisoner at Cajamarca, shortly after the civil war.
The last Inca state is conquered and the last ruler, Túpac Amaru, is executed.

mapNote.en: From 1540 the map shows only a small area, up to and including 1571.

The sources give 1438–1533 for the empire and 1572 for the fall of the last Inca state. The map shows the Inca Empire 1440–1571, from 1540 only a small area. For 1294–1439 the map shows its predecessor, the Kingdom of Cusco.

summary.en: Chimor was the kingdom of the Chimú culture on the northern coast of Peru, with its capital at Chan Chan. According to Wikipedia it was the largest kingdom of its period, and at its greatest extent it covered about 1,000 km of coast. The Inca Empire conquered it around 1470.

text.en: The Chimú culture arose around the year 900 on the northern coast of Peru, after the Moche culture. According to Chimú oral tradition the first ruler, Taycanamo, arrived by sea on a raft and founded Chan Chan. This is a legend and not an attested date.

The Inca ruler Topa Inca Yupanqui defeated the ruler of Chimor, Minchançaman, who was taken to Cusco. The sources differ on the year: Wikipedia gives around 1470 for the conquest, but also writes that it began in the 1470s and was nearly complete in 1493.
Chan Chan.

mapNote.en: The sources differ: Wikipedia gives about 900–1470 and Wikidata 850 or 900 to 1470. The map shows Chimor in 911–1481, as in Cliopatria. Cliopatria has two entries, Chimor (911–1187) and Chimu Empire (1188–1481); here they are shown as one state, since the sources mention no break. The borders are Cliopatria's estimate and not known state borders, and before 1202 in particular a large part of the area lies in the sea. How far south the kingdom reached is disputed according to Wikipedia.

summary.en: The Purépecha Empire was the state of the Purépecha people in present-day Mexico, with its capital Tzintzuntzan on Lake Pátzcuaro. It was a contemporary and rival of the Aztec Empire, and when the Spaniards came it was, according to Wikipedia, the second-largest state in Mesoamerica. It is also called the Tarascan Empire, a name that probably comes from the Spaniards and that is unpopular in most Purépecha communities.

text.en: According to the Relación de Michoacán, a chronicle from around 1540 based on oral tradition, King Tariácuri founded the state. Around 1300 he made his first conquests from the city of Pátzcuaro. The dates are those of tradition and are not certain.

After the fall of the Aztec Empire a Spanish force under Cristóbal de Olid reached Tzintzuntzan in 1522, and the Purépecha army did not fight. King Tangáxuan II submitted but kept a large degree of autonomy. Nuño de Guzmán had him executed on 14 February 1530, and the state was placed under New Spain.
Tzintzuntzan.
Wikipedia gives 75,000 km² in 1450 and 1.5 million inhabitants in 1519.

mapNote.en: The sources give about 1300–1530 (Wikipedia and Wikidata). The map shows the state in 1305–1533, as in Cliopatria, where the entry is called Michoacán. Before 1440 Cliopatria's area lies south of Lake Pátzcuaro, where the sources place the core of the state: the capital Tzintzuntzan lies about 84 km outside the area in 1305–1428 and about 33 km outside it in 1429–1439. For 1450 Cliopatria has 49,787 km², Wikipedia 75,000 km². The borders are Cliopatria's estimate and not known state borders.

summary.en: The Songhai Empire was a state in the western Sahel in the 15th and 16th centuries, one of the largest empires in African history. It had its capital at Gao on the Niger River and controlled the trading cities of Timbuktu and Djenné.

text.en: A Songhai state existed around Gao as early as the 11th century and was later subject to the Mali Empire. When Mali weakened, Songhai grew. The sources differ about when the empire began: Wikipedia gives the 1430s or 1464, World History Encyclopedia about 1460.
After civil war the Moroccan sultan Ahmad al-Mansur sent an army under Judar Pasha. Songhai lost the Battle of Tondibi in 1591, and Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné were sacked.
Gao.

Sonni Ali (1464–1492) conquered Timbuktu in 1468 and Djenné in 1475. Askia Muhammad, Askia the Great (1493–1528), carried out reforms and made the pilgrimage to Mecca. Askia Ishaq II (1588–1592) was the last.
About 1.4 million km² in 1528. World History Encyclopedia calls it the largest empire in West Africa ever.
Songhai, Tuareg, Arabic, Mande languages, Fula, Hausa and Mooré. Sunni Islam and traditional African religions.
The empire profited from trade across the Sahara, where gold and ivory were exchanged for, among other things, salt. Six of the empire's nine rulers were deposed or died a violent death.
Sonni Ali makes Gao the capital and conquers large parts of the weakened Mali Empire.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire from 1463.

text.en: Songhai conquers the trading cities of Timbuktu and Djenné.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much larger from 1475.

text.en: Askia Muhammad overthrows Sonni Ali's son and carries out political and economic reforms. He introduces Islamic law and makes the pilgrimage to Mecca.
The Moroccan army defeats Songhai with the help of gunpowder weapons, and the empire falls apart.

mapNote.en: After 1595 the map shows only a small area, up to and including 1608.
The sources differ about the start (the 1430s, 1464 or about 1460) but agree about the fall in 1591. The map shows the Songhai Empire 1463–1608, from 1595 only a small area.

summary.en: The Mughal Empire was an empire in South Asia that at its height stretched from Afghanistan and Kashmir to Assam, Bangladesh and the Deccan Plateau. It was founded in 1526 and dissolved by the British in 1857.

text.en: Babur, a Timurid prince from the Fergana Valley in Central Asia, defeated the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi, at Panipat in 1526.

After Aurangzeb's death in 1707 the empire weakened, and by 1760 only the area around Delhi remained. After the rebellion of 1857 the last emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, was deposed by the British East India Company and exiled to Rangoon.
Agra, Delhi, Fatehpur Sikri (1571–1585) and Lahore (1586–1598). From 1639 the capital was in Delhi.
Babur (1526–1530), Humayun, Akbar (1556–1605), Shah Jahan (1628–1658) and Aurangzeb (1658–1707), under whom the empire became largest.
About 4 million km² in 1690, under Aurangzeb.
Persian was the official language. Sunni Islam was the state religion, but most of the inhabitants were Hindus.
The wealth was built on taxes on agriculture, paid in silver coins. The Mughals' buildings, such as the Taj Mahal, the Red Fort and Humayun's Tomb, are today World Heritage Sites.

The lion and the sun. The Mughal emperors' most important banner, the alam, was green with the lion and the sun. The English clergyman Edward Terry saw it under Jahangir: a crouching lion in front of the sun, carried on an elephant when the emperor travelled. The Mughals said that the banner went back to Timur. Wikipedia's article on the banners has few source references.
Babur defeats the Sultan of Delhi and takes over the plains of northern India.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire from 1529.

text.en: The rebel Sher Shah Suri drives Humayun into exile in Persia. Humayun returns in 1555 but dies the year after.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much smaller in 1540–1555.

text.en: Akbar reigns for almost fifty years and introduces taxes on agriculture that become the basis of the empire's wealth.
Under Shah Jahan art and architecture flourish at court.
Under Aurangzeb, who wages war in the Deccan in 1680–1707, the empire reaches its greatest size.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire at its largest in 1691–1708.

text.en: The Persian ruler Nader Shah sacks Delhi and takes the Mughals' treasures with him. The empire shrinks rapidly.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much smaller from 1741.

text.en: After the rebellion of 1857 the British depose Bahadur Shah Zafar.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire up to and including 1858.
The sources give 1526–1857. The map shows the Mughal Empire 1529–1858.

summary.en: The Safavid Empire was one of Iran's largest and longest-lived empires, ruled by the Safavid dynasty in 1501–1736. The Safavids made Twelver Shia Islam the state religion in Iran.

text.en: The Safavids were originally a Sufi order in Ardabil. Shah Ismail I founded the empire in 1501, with the support of the Qizilbash, Turkmen tribes that made up the main part of the army.
Afghans took the capital Isfahan in 1722, and some historians count that as the end of the empire. The dynasty was restored for a short time, but the last shah, Abbas III, reigned only until 1736.
Ismail I (1501–1524), Abbas I, who moved the capital to Isfahan in 1598, and Abbas III (1732–1736), the last.
About 2.9 million km² in 1630: all of present-day Iran, Azerbaijan and Armenia, eastern Georgia, Iraq and parts of neighbouring countries.
Persian was the official language, but Turkic was also spoken at court. Twelver Shia Islam was the state religion; in the empire there were also Sunnis, Zoroastrians and Christians.
In Isfahan, after 1598, some of the Safavid era's best-known buildings were built, among them the Shah Mosque, which was completed in 1630.

The lion and the sun were found on the Safavids' copper coins, banners and works of art. The Safavids used several banners, but under Abbas I (1588–1629) the lion and the sun had become one of the most common emblems, so it is most securely attested for the later part of the empire. The Safavids interpreted it as the two pillars of state and religion.
Ismail I takes power with Tabriz as the capital and makes Twelver Shia Islam the state religion.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire from 1502 and much larger from 1507.

text.en: Abbas I moves the capital from Qazvin to Isfahan, where great mosques and a new palace are built.
Afghans take Isfahan. The empire falls apart, and some historians count that as the end.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much smaller from 1721 and only a small area from 1727.

text.en: The last Safavid shah, Abbas III, reigns until 1736.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire up to and including 1737.
The sources give 1501–1736; some historians count the end as 1722. The map shows the Safavid Empire 1502–1737.

summary.en: The Ming dynasty ruled China in 1368–1644, after the Mongol Yuan Empire. It was the last imperial dynasty in China led by Han Chinese. Under the Ming the Forbidden City was built and the Great Wall of China took its present form.

text.en: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaimed himself emperor in Nanjing in January 1368 and took the name Hongwu.

Crop failures, floods and an epidemic weakened the empire. The rebel leader Li Zicheng took Beijing in 1644, and the last emperor took his own life. The Manchus then took power and founded the Qing dynasty. Relatives of the Ming emperors held out in southern China, the Southern Ming, until 1662.
Nanjing and Beijing. Emperor Yongle made Beijing the capital in 1420 (another source says 1421).

Hongwu (1368–1398) founded the dynasty. Yongle (1402/1403–1424) built the Forbidden City and sent Admiral Zheng He on seven great voyages across the Indian Ocean, all the way to Arabia and East Africa.
About 6.5 million km² in 1450.
Mandarin was the official language. Worship of Heaven, Daoism, Confucianism, Buddhism and folk religion, but also Islam and Catholicism.
In the 16th century silver from South America poured in through trade with the Portuguese, Spaniards and Dutch, and new crops such as maize and potatoes came to China.
Hongwu proclaims himself emperor in Nanjing after the fall of the Yuan Empire.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Ming dynasty from 1375.

text.en: Emperor Yongle sends an enormous fleet under Zheng He to countries around the Indian Ocean.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire at its largest in 1415–1428.

text.en: Yongle moves the capital from Nanjing to Beijing, closer to the border with the Mongols, and builds the Forbidden City.
Emperor Yingzong is taken prisoner. After that the fleet decays, and the wall is extended and fortified.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire smaller from 1440 and 1450.

text.en: Li Zicheng's rebel army takes Beijing. Ming relatives continue to rule parts of southern China.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Ming dynasty up to and including 1644 and the Southern Ming in 1645–1682.

The sources give 1368–1644. The Southern Ming held out until 1662 according to Wikipedia and until 1661 according to Wikidata, but the map (Cliopatria) shows the Southern Ming up to and including 1682. The map shows the Ming dynasty 1375–1644.

summary.en: The Qing dynasty was China's last imperial dynasty, led by Manchus. It ruled from 1636/1644 to 1912 and laid the foundation for the borders of modern China. The Qing controlled more land than any other Chinese dynasty.

text.en: Nurhaci united the Jurchen tribes (later called Manchus) and founded the Later Jin in 1616. His son Hong Taiji was proclaimed emperor of the Qing in Shenyang in 1636. The Qing took Beijing in 1644, which is usually counted as the dynasty's start in China.
After losses in the Opium Wars the Qing were forced to sign unequal treaties. The Xinhai Revolution broke out in October 1911, and the child emperor Puyi abdicated on 12 February 1912.
Beijing (from 1644).
Kangxi (1661–1722), who reigned longer than any other Chinese emperor, and Qianlong (1735–1796), when the empire was at its most powerful.
About 14.7 million km² in 1790, from the Sea of Japan to the Pamir Mountains. The empire was also the world's most populous state, with over 426 million inhabitants in 1907.
Manchu, Mandarin and Mongolian were official languages.
In 1645 all adult Han Chinese men were forced to wear the Manchus' hairstyle with a shaved forehead and a queue, or face the death penalty.

The Dragon Flag, a blue dragon on a yellow field with a red pearl. The map shows the triangular form in 1862–1888 and the rectangular form in 1889–1911. The rectangular version became China's first national flag. Before 1862 the map instead shows the empire's dragon emblem.
The Ming dynasty has fallen to rebels. General Wu Sangui lets the Qing army in through the Shanhai Pass, and the Qing take over Beijing.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Qing from 1645.

text.en: The resistance from Ming loyalists and the Revolt of the Three Feudatories is crushed, and the Qing rule all of China.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much larger from 1683.

text.en: Qianlong leads ten great campaigns, and the empire reaches its greatest size.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire at its largest from 1757.

text.en: Britain defeats the Qing, and China is forced to open up to foreign trade.
A great rebellion shakes the empire for fourteen years.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire smaller in the 1860s.

text.en: After the Xinhai Revolution of 1911 the child emperor Puyi abdicates, and China becomes a republic.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire up to and including 1911.
The sources give 1636 or 1644 as the start and 1912 as the end. The map shows the Qing dynasty 1645–1911.

summary.en: The Spanish Empire was a colonial empire that existed in 1492–1976 and ruled large parts of the Americas, but also areas in Africa, Asia, Oceania and Europe. It was called “the empire on which the sun never sets”.

text.en: The empire is counted from Christopher Columbus's voyage to the Americas in 1492. Over more than three centuries it spread across the Caribbean, half of South America, most of Central America and large parts of North America.

By the middle of the 1820s Spain had lost Mexico, Central America and South America. After the Spanish–American War in 1898 Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines and Guam were lost. Spain left Western Sahara last, in 1976.
The court moved around until 1561, then Madrid (except 1601–1606, when it was in Valladolid).
The Catholic Monarchs (1492–1516) and Philip II (1556–1598), who had the Philippines colonised from 1565. In 1700 the House of Bourbon took over with Philip V.
About 13.7 million km² in 1780.

The Spaniards conquered the Aztec Empire with the help of Indigenous allies. War and disease decimated the Indigenous populations, and in the silver mines of Potosí the Indigenous population was forced to work (mit'a). The Mapuche in southern Chile resisted for several hundred years.
Spanish and Catholicism, which was the state religion. Many Indigenous languages disappeared as Spanish spread.

The Pillars of Hercules with the ribbon Plus Ultra, “further beyond”. Charles I (Emperor Charles V) took them as his personal emblem in 1516, when he became king of Spain, and they became part of Spain's arms, alluding to the discovery of the Americas. They were used in Spanish and Habsburg propaganda. Spain's military flag, the Cross of Burgundy, was passed over because it is a cross.
Columbus's voyage becomes the beginning of Spain's empire in the Americas.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire from 1516.

text.en: Hernán Cortés and his Indigenous allies conquer the Aztec Empire.
The Spaniards conquer the Inca Empire. The silver from Potosí, found in 1545, makes the Spanish crown rich.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire twice as large from 1540.

text.en: Philip II conquers Portugal, and the two crowns are united until 1640.

mapNote.en: The map counts Portugal and its colonies as part of the Spanish Empire in 1582–1639.

text.en: The Spanish Empire is at its largest in the late 18th century and early 19th century.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire at its largest in 1778–1810.

text.en: The colonies in the Americas break free, and by the middle of the 1820s Spain has lost the mainland.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much smaller from 1822.

text.en: Spain loses Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines and Guam.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire up to and including 1931.
The sources give 1492–1976. The map shows the Spanish Empire with Spain 1516–1931; in 1582–1639 Portugal and its colonies are included.

summary.en: The Portuguese Empire was the first and longest-lived of the European colonial empires, 1415–1999. It consisted of Brazil, areas in Africa and a chain of ports and trading posts from Africa to Japan.

text.en: Portugal conquered Ceuta in North Africa in 1415. Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498 and Pedro Álvares Cabral reached Brazil in 1500.

Brazil became independent in 1822. The colonial war in Africa lasted 1961–1974, and after the Carnation Revolution in 1974 Portugal left the African colonies. Macao was handed over to China last, in 1999.
Lisbon (Rio de Janeiro 1808–1821).

Philip II of Spain took the Portuguese crown in 1580. During 60 years in union with Spain the Portuguese colonies were attacked by Spain's enemies, and the empire began slowly to shrink. Portugal became independent again in 1640.

The slave trade was a large part of the empire's trade: people were taken from West and southern Africa to work on plantations on the Atlantic islands and in the Americas. Well into the 20th century forced labour was kept in the colonies.
Portuguese and Roman Catholic Christianity.
In 1571 a chain of ports linked Lisbon with Nagasaki in Japan. Gold, ivory, silk, porcelain and spices were shipped around the world.

The armillary sphere, a model of the celestial circles. It was Manuel I's personal emblem in the late 15th century, and when he used it on documents, buildings and flags it became an emblem of Portugal and its dominion over the seas. It is associated with the Portuguese voyages of discovery and remained after Manuel's death. It is today on Portugal's flag.
Portugal conquers Ceuta, a port for the trans-Saharan trade in gold and slaves.
Vasco da Gama reaches India, and Cabral reaches Brazil on the way there.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire from 1502.

text.en: The Portuguese take Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate and make it a base in India.
Spain's king takes the Portuguese crown, and the colonies are attacked by the Dutch, English and French.

mapNote.en: The map counts Portugal and most of the colonies as part of the Spanish Empire in 1582–1639.

text.en: The empire's most valuable colony breaks free.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much smaller from 1824.

text.en: Portugal's colonies along the African coast grow inland.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire larger from 1885, up to and including 1910.

text.en: The last territory, Macao, is handed over to China.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1415–1999. The map shows the Portuguese Empire with Portugal in 1502–1975; in 1582–1639 only some colonies, since the rest is part of the Spanish Empire. In 1911–1975 it is Cliopatria's Portuguese Republic and Estado Novo, which both include the colonies. From 1976 Portugal is shown as a country of its own.

summary.en: Russia grew from the tsardom around Moscow into an empire across the whole of northern Eurasia. In the 19th century it covered roughly a sixth of the Earth's land area.

text.en: Ivan IV was crowned tsar in 1547, and the tsardom became the first phase of the tsars' Russia. Peter the Great proclaimed the Russian Empire in 1721, after the victory over Sweden.
During the First World War heavy losses and shortages of food led to the February Revolution in 1917. Nicholas II abdicated and Russia was proclaimed a republic.
Moscow (1547–1712) and Saint Petersburg (1712–1917, except a few years in the 1720s and 1730s when the capital was in Moscow again).
Ivan IV, Peter the Great (in power from 1689), Catherine the Great (1762–1796), Alexander II, who freed 23 million serfs in 1861, and Nicholas II, the last.
About 22.8 million km² in 1895, from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific. Russia also colonised Alaska in 1799–1867 and then sold it to the United States.

From 1581 Cossacks and fur traders pushed east through Siberia to the Pacific. According to the source the Indigenous peoples offered little resistance. Later the empire pursued a harsh policy of Russification in Poland, Finland and other border areas.
Russian was the official language. Russian Orthodox Christianity was the state religion; in 1897 11 per cent were also Muslims and 4 per cent Jews.

The double-headed eagle has been Russia's coat of arms since the 15th century, under Ivan III (1462–1505). After the fall of Constantinople in 1453 the grand princes of Moscow saw themselves as Byzantium's heirs, and the eagle has Byzantine models. It was the arms of both the tsardom and the empire.
Ivan IV becomes the first Russian ruler to be crowned tsar.

mapNote.en: The map shows the tsardom from 1547.

text.en: The merchant family Stroganov hires the Cossack leader Yermak for an expedition into western Siberia. The Russians reach the Pacific in the middle of the 17th century.

mapNote.en: The map shows the tsardom growing sharply from 1595 and especially in the 1630s.

text.en: The transition from the Rurik to the Romanov dynasty is marked by war and chaos.
After the victory in the Great Northern War, Peter the Great proclaims the Russian Empire.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Russian Empire from 1721.

text.en: Alexander I helps to defeat Napoleon.
Alexander II frees 23 million serfs.
Russia sells Alaska to the United States for 7.2 million dollars.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire somewhat smaller from 1868.

text.en: Nicholas II abdicates, and Russia becomes a republic.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire up to and including 1916.
The sources give 1547–1721 for the tsardom and 1721–1917 for the empire. The map shows the tsardom 1547–1720 and the empire 1721–1916.

summary.en: Sweden gradually came together as one realm during the Viking Age and the Middle Ages. During the Swedish Empire period, 1611–1721, Sweden was a European great power that controlled large parts of the Baltic region. It ended when Sweden lost the Great Northern War. In 1814–1905 Sweden was in union with Norway, and since 1905 the country has been a kingdom of its own.

text.en: In the centuries after about 800 Sweden gradually came together as one realm. Olof Skötkonung, who lived until about 1020, was the first Christian king and the first known to have ruled over the different peoples. The Kalmar Union between the Scandinavian countries was formed in 1397 and lasted until Gustav Vasa broke it when he took power in the War of Liberation, which ended in 1523.

The Swedish Empire period is counted from 1611, when Gustavus Adolphus became king. After the victories in the Thirty Years' War Sweden gained territories in northern Germany at the Peace of Westphalia in 1648.

label.en: How the Swedish Empire period ended

text.en: Charles XII lost the Battle of Poltava in 1709. When he died in 1718 the realm was greatly weakened, and at the Peace of Nystad in 1721 Sweden lost large territories. Finland was ceded to Russia in 1809 and Swedish Pomerania after the Napoleonic Wars.

At the Treaty of Kiel on 14 January 1814 Denmark-Norway had to cede Norway to the King of Sweden. Norway declared itself independent and adopted a constitution of its own on 17 May 1814, but after a short war and the Convention of Moss the Storting elected Sweden's King Charles XIII king of Norway on 4 November 1814. The countries had a common king and foreign policy but their own constitutions, parliaments, armies and currencies. The campaign against Norway in 1814 was the last time Sweden was at war.

The Storting declared the union dissolved on 7 June 1905, and Sweden accepted it on 26 October. Sweden was officially neutral in both world wars, but its neutrality during the Second World War is debated. The country joined the EU in 1995 and, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, NATO on 7 March 2024.
Stockholm, the official capital from 1634. The city is first mentioned in writing in 1252.
Gustavus Adolphus (1611–1632), Christina (1632–1654), Charles X Gustav (1654–1660) and Charles XII.
Sweden was at its most powerful during the war of 1655–1660, when Denmark-Norway was forced to give up a third of its land at the Peace of Roskilde in 1658. The source gives no area.
Swedish. The Church of Sweden was the state church.
Sweden also had colonies, such as New Sweden on the Delaware River in North America, founded in 1638.

Three Crowns, two above and one below, is Sweden's national coat of arms. The oldest known coat of arms with three crowns as an emblem for Sweden is a painted frieze in Avignon from the 1330s, under Magnus Eriksson, and the following kings kept it. During the Swedish Empire period it had long been the realm's emblem.
The Swedish Empire period begins.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Swedish Empire from 1612.

title.en: Gustavus Adolphus is killed in battle

text.en: The king dies during the Thirty Years' War, and Christina becomes queen.

mapNote.en: The map shows the realm at its largest in 1632–1635.

text.en: Sweden gains territories in northern Germany.
Denmark-Norway has to give up a third of its land, and Sweden is at its most powerful.
Charles XII's campaign in Russia ends in a great defeat, and Sweden's expansion is over.
Sweden loses large territories after the Great Northern War, and the Swedish Empire period is over.

mapNote.en: The map shows the realm smaller in 1718–1720. From 1722 it is called Sweden on the map.

text.en: Sweden cedes Finland to Russia.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area decreasing from about 790,000 to 464,000 km² in 1809.

text.en: After the Treaty of Kiel and a short war the Storting elects Sweden's king king of Norway on 4 November 1814. The union is a personal union with a common king and foreign policy.

mapNote.en: The map shows Norway as a country of its own in 1814 and the Sweden-Norway union from 1815.

text.en: The Storting declares the union dissolved on 7 June 1905, and Sweden accepts it on 26 October. The dissolution takes place peacefully.

mapNote.en: The map shows Sweden without Norway from 1905.

text.en: Sweden joins the European Union.
After Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 Sweden applies for membership, and becomes a member of NATO on 7 March 2024.

mapNote.en: The map shows Sweden from 980. In 1402–1501 the map data (Cliopatria) counts the area as part of the Kalmar Union, so no Sweden is shown there. The sources give the Swedish Empire period as 1611–1721; it ended with the Peace of Nystad in 1721. The map (Cliopatria) calls Sweden “Swedish Empire” all the way to 1814. Here the realm is therefore called the Swedish Empire up to and including 1721 and Sweden 1722–1814, with the map data's borders, that is Sweden with Finland and Pomerania after the Swedish Empire period. The union with Norway is shown 1815–1904 (the sources: 1814–1905) and Sweden from 1905.

summary.en: The Habsburg Empire was a collection of empires, kingdoms and principalities ruled by the House of Habsburg, with Vienna as its capital. It was called the Austrian Empire from 1804 and Austria-Hungary from 1867.

text.en: The Habsburgs received the Duchy of Austria in 1282. Ferdinand became king of Bohemia and Hungary in 1526, after the king of Hungary fell against the Ottomans at Mohács. The sources differ about the start: Wikipedia gives 1282, Wikidata 1526.
The empire fell apart at the end of the First World War and was dissolved in 1918.
Vienna, except 1583–1611, when the capital was in Prague.

Maximilian I gained the Netherlands through marriage in 1482. Charles V also ruled Spain and its colonies but abdicated in 1556, and the empire was divided between his son Philip II of Spain and his brother Ferdinand I. Through Maria Theresa's marriage the dynasty continued as the House of Habsburg-Lorraine after 1740.
The empire was a union of crowns held together by a common monarch. It comprised the Austrian hereditary lands, the Bohemian lands, Hungary and areas conquered from the Ottoman Empire.
Roman Catholic Christianity was the official religion.

The double-headed eagle was the arms of the Holy Roman Emperor from 1433, and from Frederick III the Habsburgs were emperors. Austria took the double-headed eagle as its own arms in 1804, shortly before the Holy Roman Empire was dissolved. The map's double-headed eagle thus stands for the Habsburgs' imperial arms.
After the Battle of Mohács Ferdinand is elected king of Bohemia and Hungary.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire larger from 1556.

text.en: The empire is divided between a Spanish and an Austrian branch of the family.
After the Battle of Vienna and the Peace of Karlowitz the empire grows at the expense of the Ottoman Empire.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much larger from 1687 and 1696.

text.en: The male line dies out, and through Maria Theresa's marriage the dynasty continues as Habsburg-Lorraine.
The Habsburg lands are united in the Austrian Empire.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Habsburg Empire up to and including 1805.
The sources differ about the start (1282 or 1526) but both give 1918 as the end. The map shows the empire 1459–1805; the Austrian Empire and Austria-Hungary are not included here.

summary.en: The Tokugawa shogunate was Japan's military government in 1603–1868. The shoguns of the Tokugawa family ruled the country from Edo, present-day Tokyo, together with the feudal lords, the daimyo, while the emperor remained in Kyoto.

text.en: Tokugawa Ieyasu won the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 and became shogun in 1603. It ended the civil wars of the Sengoku period.

The shogunate weakened from 1853 and was overthrown by the emperor's supporters in the Meiji Restoration in 1868, when the fifteenth shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu resigned. Tokugawa loyalists fought on until June 1869.
Edo (the shogun's seat). The emperor's palace was in Heian-kyō (Kyoto).
Tokugawa Ieyasu (shogun 1603–1605), his son Hidetada and grandson Iemitsu.
With the sakoku policy Japan was closed to most foreigners, and Japanese were not allowed to leave the country. Christianity was banned, and only the Dutch were allowed to trade, in Nagasaki.
Japanese. Buddhism and Confucianism were state religions.
During the long peace the economy and the cities grew, and the merchants and ukiyo culture gained a larger place.

Three hollyhock leaves (aoi) in a circle, the Tokugawa family's coat of arms (mon). During the Edo period it was forbidden for others to use the shogunate's hollyhock crest, as well as the imperial house's chrysanthemum.
Tokugawa Ieyasu wins and in 1603 becomes shogun.

mapNote.en: The map shows Tokugawa Japan from 1600.

text.en: The founder dies, but the Tokugawa family keeps power for another 250 years.
Japan closes itself to foreigners and forbids Japanese to travel abroad.
The shogunate weakens and in 1854 signs the Convention of Kanagawa.
The shogun resigns and imperial rule is restored.

mapNote.en: The map shows Tokugawa Japan up to and including 1869.
The sources give 1603–1868. The map shows Tokugawa Japan 1600–1869.

summary.en: The French colonial empire consisted of the colonies, protectorates and mandates that were ruled from France. The first empire, in the Americas and India, was almost entirely lost by 1814. The second empire, which the map shows, began with the conquest of Algiers in 1830 and before the First World War was the second largest in the world, after the British.

text.en: France founded colonies in the Americas, the Caribbean and India from the 16th century, but lost most of them after the Seven Years' War and sold Louisiana to the United States in 1803. The second colonial empire began with the invasion of Algiers in 1830 and was mostly built up after 1850, above all in Africa, Indochina and the Pacific.

After the Second World War independence movements challenged French rule. France lost the wars in Indochina (1946–1954) and Algeria (1954–1962). Tunisia and Morocco became independent in 1956 and almost all other African colonies in 1960. Djibouti became independent in 1977 and Vanuatu, the last, in 1980. Some territories are today French departments and territories.
Paris.

The rule was justified by a “civilising mission” that was to spread the French language and French institutions. In the largest colonies the natives until 1946 were “French subjects” with different rights from French citizens; in Algeria only 3,000–6,000 Muslims gained citizenship between 1830 and 1946. According to one estimate 825,000 Algerians died during the conquest up to 1875.

Abdelkader fought the French in western Algeria until 1847, and the Mokrani Revolt of 1871–1872 spread across large parts of the country. In Morocco the Zaian offered armed resistance in 1914–1921, and Abd el-Krim's Republic of the Rif was defeated by France and Spain in 1926. After 1945 France put down the protests in Sétif, where between 6,000 and 45,000 Algerians were killed according to estimates, and the uprising in Madagascar in 1947.

In 1870 the French territories outside Europe covered about 1 million km² with over 5 million inhabitants. According to the 1936 census 69.1 million people lived in the empire outside France, of whom 25.5 million were in sub-Saharan Africa, 23.2 million in East and Southeast Asia and 16.1 million in North Africa.

The map shows France's royal white flag in 1815–1829 and the tricolour from 1830. The tricolour – blue, white and red – was introduced in 1794 and was the flag of the empires and the republics. During the Bourbon Restoration the white royal flag was used instead.
France lands 37,000 soldiers, takes Algiers and deposes the dey. The second colonial empire begins. All of Algeria is conquered only in the early 20th century.

mapNote.en: The map shows Algeria from 1830. The map calls France the kingdom in 1815–1847.

text.en: France sends 35,000 soldiers from Algeria and makes Tunisia a protectorate with the Treaty of Bardo. By the turn of the century France has taken control of large parts of North, West and Central Africa and Madagascar.

mapNote.en: The map shows the increase in 1880 and 1885.

text.en: With the Treaty of Huế in 1883 Tonkin and Annam become French protectorates. Together with Cambodia and Cochinchina they form French Indochina in 1887. Laos is added in 1893.

mapNote.en: The map shows French territories in Indochina already from 1860.

text.en: France wants to create a contiguous west–east axis across Africa, but withdraws after meeting a British force at Fashoda in Sudan. Britain keeps Egypt, and France becomes the dominant power in Morocco, which becomes a protectorate in 1912.

mapNote.en: The map shows the large increases in Africa in 1895 and 1905, from about 2.4 to 11.5 million km².

text.en: After the First World War France receives mandates over the former Ottoman territories Syria and Lebanon and over most of the former German colonies Togo and Cameroon. These are the last major additions.

After the fall of France the Vichy regime and the Free French under Charles de Gaulle fight over the colonies, sometimes with weapons. By 1943 all colonies except the Japanese-controlled Indochina have gone over to the Free French.

mapNote.en: The map shows the colonies under the Vichy regime in 1940–1942 and lacks France and the colonies in 1943–1944.

title.en: Điện Biên Phủ and the Algerian War

text.en: The Viet Minh defeat the French at Điện Biên Phủ, and France leaves Indochina after the Geneva Accords. The same year the Algerian War begins, which ends with Algeria's independence in 1962. Tunisia and Morocco become independent in 1956 and almost all other African colonies in 1960.

mapNote.en: The map data ends in 1957 and does not show the independence of 1960 and 1962.

The source counts the second colonial empire from 1830; most colonies became independent in 1954–1962 and the last in 1977–1980. The map shows France with colonies 1815–1957 and lacks the years 1943–1944. The map's parts are named after France's form of government (the kingdom, the Second Republic, the Second Empire, the Third Republic, the Vichy regime and the Fourth Republic).

summary.en: The Dutch colonial empire consisted of trading posts and colonies that were first ruled by trading companies, the East India Company (VOC, 1602–1799) and the West India Company, and then by the state. The most important area was the Dutch East Indies, present-day Indonesia.

text.en: In the late 16th century Dutch trading expeditions sailed to Asia to buy spices. In 1602 the States General merged the trading companies into the East India Company, which received a monopoly on trade with Asia and the right to build forts, conclude treaties and wage war. The West India Company was founded in 1621 for the Americas and West Africa.

Japan occupied the Dutch East Indies in 1942. After Japan's surrender in 1945 Sukarno and Hatta proclaimed Indonesia's independence, and after four and a half years of war the Netherlands recognised Indonesia in December 1949. Western New Guinea was handed over in 1962 or 1963 (the sources give different years), and Suriname became independent in 1975. Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten are today self-governing countries within the Kingdom.
Batavia (Jakarta), which the East India Company built in 1619.

The Company took power by force: on the Banda Islands 44 local leaders were killed in 1621, and captured Bandanese were sold as slaves. The Cultivation System from 1830 forced the peasants of Java to grow export crops on a fifth of their land. It gave large profits but led to famine and disease in the 1840s. Slavery in the Caribbean colonies was abolished only in 1863.

For a long time many areas were independent, among them Aceh, Bali, Lombok and Borneo. The Netherlands waged war against the indigenous states: the Padri War (1821–1838), the Java War (1825–1830) and the Aceh War, which began in 1873 and ended with the Acehnese surrender in 1912. The whole archipelago came under direct colonial rule only in 1901–1910.

Around 1652 the empire had colonies or trading posts in North America, the Caribbean, South America, West and South Africa, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Japan and Taiwan. The Dutch East Indies were largest in the early 20th century, when western New Guinea was occupied.

The bundle of seven arrows from the Netherlands' coat of arms. The States General of the United Netherlands (1581–1795) had a lion with a crown, sword and bundle of arrows; the arrows stand for the seven provinces of the Union of Utrecht. The Kingdom took the lion with the arrows into its coat of arms in 1815. The map shows only the bundle of arrows. For the years 1795–1815 (the Batavian Republic) the emblem is not attested in the source.

title.en: The East India Company is founded

text.en: The States General merge the trading companies into the East India Company (VOC), with a monopoly on trade with Asia. The Company may build forts, conclude treaties and wage war, and attacks Portugal's trading posts.

mapNote.en: The map shows the first stations in Asia from 1600.

text.en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen attacks Banten and Jayakarta, burns Jayakarta and builds Batavia on the ruins. Batavia becomes the Company's centre in Asia.
The Company founds a provisioning station for ships at the Cape of Good Hope. The colony grows, and the Khoikhoi and San peoples lose their lands.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Cape Colony from 1653.

text.en: The French revolutionary army invades and makes the country the Batavian Republic. Britain takes Dutch colonies in Asia, South Africa and the Caribbean. The Company is dissolved, and its territories become the Dutch East Indies in 1800. After 1814 the Netherlands gets back most of it, but not the Cape Colony and Ceylon.

mapNote.en: In 1811–1814 the map shows only the colonies, without the Netherlands, which was then ruled directly from France. The British conquered Java in 1811, but the map shows the island as Dutch.

text.en: The peasants of Java must grow export crops such as indigo, coffee and sugar on a fifth of their land. The profit corresponds to roughly half of the Dutch state's revenue, but the system leads to famine and disease. It is abolished in 1870.
The Netherlands invades Aceh in northern Sumatra and meets guerrilla resistance until 1912. From 1901 to 1910 the rest of the archipelago is placed under direct colonial rule.

mapNote.en: The map shows a large increase in 1873, from about 0.85 to 1.3 million km².

text.en: Japan occupies the colony in 1942. Two days after Japan's surrender in 1945 Sukarno and Hatta proclaim Indonesia's independence. The Netherlands sends about 220,000 soldiers but recognises Indonesia's independence in December 1949.

mapNote.en: In 1941–1942 the map shows only the colony and lacks the years 1943–1944. The map data ends in 1949 and does not show western New Guinea, Suriname and the Caribbean islands.

The source counts the empire from the early 17th century to Suriname's independence in 1975. The map shows the Netherlands with colonies 1582–1949; after 1949 Cliopatria has only the Netherlands. The map lacks the years 1943–1944 and shows the colonies without the Netherlands in 1811–1814 and 1941–1942.

summary.en: The German Empire was formed in 1871, when the southern German states joined the North German Confederation under Prussian leadership. It became continental Europe's largest economy and from 1884 acquired colonies in Africa and the Pacific, in one year the third largest colonial empire after the British and the French.

text.en: The empire was founded on 18 January 1871. The same day Prussia's King Wilhelm I was proclaimed German emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, during the siege of Paris in the Franco-Prussian War. The empire consisted of 25 states; Prussia was the largest and had three fifths of the population.

In November 1918, with revolution in the country and the army in retreat, the emperor and all the German princes abdicated, and on 9 November a republic was proclaimed. By the Treaty of Versailles in 1919 Germany lost all colonies, which became mandates under the League of Nations.
Berlin. Otto von Bismarck was imperial chancellor in 1871–1890.
German South West Africa (Namibia), Togo, Cameroon and German East Africa (mainland Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi), New Guinea and islands in the Pacific, and later Kiautschou in China and Samoa.

The Herero and Nama rose in revolt in German South West Africa in 1904. It was put down in a genocide in which between 50 and 70 per cent of the Herero people perished. When the Maji Maji Rebellion in German East Africa was put down in 1905–1907 an estimated 100,000 people died, many of them of starvation after the German troops' scorched-earth tactics.
About 41 million inhabitants in 1871 and 68 million in 1913. The empire in Europe was 540,858 km² in 1910.

The imperial eagle, a black eagle with one head and an imperial crown. It was introduced at the proclamation of the emperor at Versailles in 1871 and drew on the medieval arms of the Holy Roman emperors, before they took the double-headed eagle. That it has only one head distinguishes it from the eagle of the German Confederation.
After the victory in the Franco-Prussian War Wilhelm I is proclaimed German emperor at Versailles on 18 January. Bismarck becomes imperial chancellor and then tries to preserve peace in Europe.

Lüderitz's trading post becomes German South West Africa in April, and in July Togo and Cameroon follow, then north-eastern New Guinea. In one year Germany becomes the third largest colonial power. The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 sets rules for the Europeans' partition of Africa.

mapNote.en: The map shows the colonies in Africa from 1885. Already in 1871–1884 Cliopatria has a small German area in Africa, about 1,900 km².

title.en: The genocide of the Herero and Nama

text.en: After rinderpest and lost grazing land the Herero and Nama rise in revolt. Germany sends about 15,000 soldiers, and the revolt is put down in a genocide. The Maji Maji Rebellion in German East Africa in 1905–1907 costs an estimated 100,000 people their lives.
Germany enters the war together with Austria-Hungary. The colonies are lost early in the war, but German forces hold out in German East Africa until the end of the war.

mapNote.en: The map shows the losses in Africa in 1915–1918.

text.en: By the Peace of Brest-Litovsk in March Germany gains large territories in the east; the Baltic region, Belarus and Ukraine are placed under German occupation administration. In November the empire collapses: the emperor abdicates, and on 9 November a republic is proclaimed.

mapNote.en: The map shows the occupied territories in 1918 and the empire for one more year, 1919.

text.en: Germany must cede all colonies. They become mandates under the League of Nations and are administered by the victorious powers.

mapNote.en: The source gives 18 January 1871–9 November 1918 and colonies 1884–1919. The map shows the empire 1871–1919. The colonies in Africa are a separate entry in Cliopatria (German Africa) and are merged here with the empire.

summary.en: The Weimar Republic was Germany's first democratic republic. It was proclaimed in November 1918, when the empire fell at the end of the First World War, and was named after the town of Weimar, where the National Assembly wrote the constitution in 1919. The republic was shaken by hyperinflation and the Great Depression and came to an end when Hitler took power in 1933.

text.en: The republic was proclaimed on 9 November 1918 by Philipp Scheidemann from the Reichstag building in Berlin. The National Assembly met in Weimar from 6 February 1919, and the constitution was adopted on 11 August 1919.

Hitler became Chancellor on 30 January 1933. The Reichstag Fire Decree of 28 February and the Enabling Act of 23 March 1933 gave him the power to govern without the Reichstag. The constitution was never formally abolished until the Allies assumed power on 5 June 1945.
Berlin.
About 62.4 million inhabitants and 468,787 km² in 1925.
Germany signs the peace treaty on 28 June. The Weimar Constitution is adopted on 11 August.
The currency collapses, and inflation peaks at the end of the year.

title.en: Member of the League of Nations

text.en: After the Locarno Treaties of 1925, Germany joins the League of Nations on 8 September 1926.
The crisis reaches Germany from October 1929. From March 1930 governments rule by the president's emergency decrees instead of relying on the Reichstag.

mapNote.en: The sources give 9 November 1918–23 March 1933 (Wikipedia) and 1918–1933 (Wikidata). The map shows the republic in 1920–1932. Cliopatria has the republic from 1920, so 1919 shows the German Empire. Cliopatria also has it up to and including 1935, but the years 1933–1935 are shown here as Nazi Germany, since the sources end the republic in 1933.

summary.en: Nazi Germany was Germany under the dictatorship of Adolf Hitler in 1933–1945. The regime persecuted Jews and other groups, annexed neighbouring countries and started the Second World War with the attack on Poland in 1939. During the war the regime murdered about six million Jews in the Holocaust and millions of other people. It fell when Germany surrendered in May 1945.

text.en: Hitler became Chancellor on 30 January 1933. The Enabling Act was passed on 23 March 1933 by 444 votes to 94 and gave the government the right to make laws without the Reichstag.

The Saar returned after a plebiscite in January 1935, and troops marched into the Rhineland on 7 March 1936. In 1938 Austria was annexed in March and the Sudetenland after the Munich Agreement in September, and in 1939 Memel. From 1939 large parts of Europe were occupied: Poland, Denmark and Norway, France, Yugoslavia and Greece, and parts of the Soviet Union. The map shows the area that Cliopatria counts to the state each year; much of it was occupied in war, not peacetime borders.

label.en: The Holocaust and other mass murders

text.en: Between 5.5 and 6 million Jews were murdered, over one million of them children. About 3.3 million of the 5.75 million captured Soviet soldiers were killed. About 220,000 Roma, roughly a quarter of Europe's Roma, and 200,000 people with disabilities were murdered.
Hitler died on 30 April 1945. The unconditional surrender was signed on 8 May 1945, and the last government was arrested on 23 May.
Berlin.
About 79.4 million inhabitants and 633,786 km² in 1939.
Hitler becomes Chancellor on 30 January, and the Enabling Act of 23 March lets the government make laws without the Reichstag.
The laws of 15 September strip Jews of their rights as citizens.
Austria is annexed in March and the Sudetenland after the Munich Agreement in September. In November at least 91 Jews are murdered in the November pogrom.
Germany attacks Poland on 1 September, and the Second World War begins.

title.en: The attack on the Soviet Union

text.en: Germany attacks the Soviet Union on 22 June.
Germany surrenders unconditionally on 8 May.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1933–1945: from 30 January 1933 to the surrender on 8 May 1945 (Wikipedia), or 15 March 1933–23 May 1945 (Wikidata). The map shows the state in 1933–1944. Cliopatria only has it from 1936; the years 1933–1935 are shown here with Cliopatria's border for the Weimar Republic. Cliopatria ends in 1944, and in 1945 the map shows the occupation zones. The area in 1938–1944 follows Cliopatria's periods and includes occupied countries.

summary.en: West Germany, the Federal Republic of Germany, was formed in 1949 from the three western occupation zones after the Second World War. It became a democracy with Bonn as its capital, joined NATO and was a founding member of the EEC. During the Cold War it was divided from East Germany, and in 1990 the two were reunified.

text.en: After the war Germany was divided into four occupation zones: a French one in the west, a British one in the north-west, an American one in the south and a Soviet one in the east. The British and American zones were merged into the Bizone, and with the French zone it became the Trizone. The Federal Republic was formed from the three western zones on 23 May 1949.
The Two Plus Four Treaty was signed on 12 September 1990, and on 3 October 1990 East Germany joined the Federal Republic. The Federal Republic continues as today's Germany.
Bonn. The Bundestag voted on 20 June 1991 to move the government to Berlin.
About 51 million inhabitants in 1950 and 63.3 million in 1990. The area was 248,717 km².
The Federal Republic is formed from the three western occupation zones on 23 May.
West Germany becomes a member of NATO on 9 May.
West Germany is a founding member of the European Economic Community on 25 March.
After the Basic Treaty with East Germany on 21 December 1972, both states become members of the UN on 18 September 1973.
East Germany joins the Federal Republic on 3 October.

mapNote.en: The sources give 23 May 1949–3 October 1990. The map shows the country in 1950–1990, as in Cliopatria. For 1945–1949 the map shows the occupation zones as parts of the United States, Britain and France, as in Cliopatria. Cliopatria also counts western Germany to the United States in 1947–1966; from 1950 this is clipped away.

summary.en: East Germany, the German Democratic Republic (GDR), was formed in 1949 from the Soviet occupation zone. It was a communist one-party state in the Eastern Bloc with East Berlin as its capital. The Berlin Wall was built in 1961 to stop people fleeing to the West. The Wall fell in 1989, and in 1990 the GDR became part of the Federal Republic.

text.en: The GDR was established on 7 October 1949 from the Soviet occupation zone, which consisted of five states: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Brandenburg, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia.
After the first free election in March 1990, the five states joined the Federal Republic on 3 October 1990, and East and West Berlin were united the same day.
East Berlin.
About 18.4 million inhabitants in 1950 and 16.1 million in 1990. The area was 108,333 km².
The GDR is established from the Soviet occupation zone on 7 October.
An uprising on 16–17 June is put down with the help of Soviet troops.
The GDR takes part when the Warsaw Pact is formed on 14 May.
