Construction of the wall between East and West Berlin begins on 13 August.
The Wall is opened on 9 November.
The five states join the Federal Republic on 3 October.

mapNote.en: The sources give 7 October 1949–3 October 1990, and the map shows the country in 1949–1990, as in Cliopatria. For 1945–1948 the map shows the Soviet zone as part of the Soviet Union, as in Cliopatria.

summary.en: Austria-Hungary was a dual monarchy in Central Europe in 1867–1918: two largely self-governing states, Austria and Hungary, with the same monarch and a common foreign, defence and monetary policy. In area it was Europe's second largest country, after Russia.

text.en: After the defeats in Italy and against Prussia in 1866 Vienna negotiated a compromise with the Hungarian leaders. Emperor Franz Joseph was crowned king of Hungary on 8 June 1867 and approved the new laws on 28 July, when the dual monarchy was formally born.

The empire fell apart in October 1918. Hungary's parliament voted on 17 October to leave the union, and on 31 October the new Hungarian government terminated the Compromise. Czechoslovakia, Poland and what became Yugoslavia were formed on the empire's territory, and on 11 November Emperor Charles withdrew from governing in Austria.
Vienna, with the court and the common ministries. Budapest was the capital of the Hungarian part.

An empire of many peoples and languages, among them German, Hungarian, Croatian, Czech, Polish, Ruthenian, Romanian, Serbian, Slovak, Slovene, Italian and Yiddish. Hungary's leaders were less willing than Austria's to share power with the minorities, and during the world war the peoples turned away from the empire and sought states of their own.
About 622,000 km² in 1905 (239,977 English square miles) and 51.4 million inhabitants in 1910.

The double-headed eagle, the Habsburgs' coat of arms, was used by the dual monarchy's common institutions from 1867. Because it was reminiscent of the Holy Roman Empire and was also the emblem of the Austrian half of the empire, the Hungarian government pushed through a new common coat of arms, introduced in 1915, which united the arms of the two halves of the empire. The double-headed eagle is thus the common emblem in 1867–1915.
Austria and Hungary become two equal states with the same monarch. Foreign policy and defence are managed jointly.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1868.

text.en: At the congress Austria-Hungary is allowed to occupy Bosnia and Herzegovina, but not annex it. The occupation requires 150,000 soldiers and several weeks of fighting.

mapNote.en: The map shows Bosnia from 1880.

text.en: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina in October. The Bosnian Crisis of 1908–1909 brings Europe to the brink of war and divides the continent into two camps.
The heir to the throne Franz Ferdinand is shot in Sarajevo on 28 June. Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia on 28 July, and the First World War begins.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area growing from about 0.68 to 0.93 million km² in 1916–1918, during the war's occupations.

text.en: Hungary leaves the union, and the other peoples form states of their own. The Republic of German-Austria is proclaimed on 12 November and the Hungarian Democratic Republic on 16 November.

mapNote.en: The source gives 1867–1918. The map shows the empire 1868–1918.

summary.en: The Japanese Empire is the period from the Meiji Restoration in 1868 to the new constitution in 1947. Japan modernised and industrialised rapidly and built up a colonial empire in East Asia: Taiwan, Korea and later great conquests in China, Southeast Asia and the Pacific.

text.en: On 3 January 1868 forces from Satsuma and Chōshū took the imperial palace in Kyoto, and the emperor proclaimed that he was taking back power. The shogunate was abolished, Edo was renamed Tokyo, and the Meiji period lasted until 1912.

The emperor announced Japan's surrender on the radio on 15 August 1945, and the war formally ended on 2 September. Japan was occupied by the Allies, and the new constitution of 3 May 1947 ended the empire.
Kyoto 1868–1869, then Tokyo.

Korea was Japanese in 1910–1945; in Korea the time is often called “the Japanese forced occupation”. Shinto was introduced in Taiwan and Korea. After the invasion of Manchuria in 1931 Japan set up the puppet state Manchukuo, with China's last emperor Puyi as head of state. In the Nanjing Massacre in 1937 an estimated 100,000–200,000 people were killed, and about 20 million Chinese, mostly civilians, were killed during the Second World War.
About 7.4 million km² in 1942. In 1940 the empire had 105.2 million inhabitants, of whom 73.1 million were in Japan proper (naichi).

The chrysanthemum crest with sixteen petals, the emperor's coat of arms (kikumon). During the Meiji period (1868–1912) no one but the emperor was allowed to use it. It is used as a national emblem, for example on Japanese passports.

The shogunate is overthrown and the emperor regains power. Under the slogan “Rich country, strong armed forces” Japan industrialises and arms itself, at a pace often counted as the fastest modernisation of any country.

Japan wins the war against China in 1894–1895 over influence in Korea. By the Treaty of Shimonoseki Japan gets Taiwan and the Liaodong Peninsula, but Russia, Germany and France force Japan to give up Liaodong.
Japan defeats Russia in the war that began in 1904 and gets southern Sakhalin (Karafuto). Korea becomes a Japanese protectorate.
Japan annexes Korea in August and rules the country for 35 years, until the surrender in 1945.

mapNote.en: The map shows Korea as Japanese from 1911.

text.en: With a false accusation of Chinese sabotage against a railway at Mukden, the Kwantung Army invades Manchuria, without the government's approval. Japan sets up the puppet state Manchukuo.

mapNote.en: The map shows Manchuria from 1932.

text.en: Japan invades China. Nanjing falls on 13 December, and in the Nanjing Massacre an estimated 100,000–200,000 people are killed.

mapNote.en: The map shows the conquered areas in China from 1938.

text.en: Japan attacks the American fleet at Pearl Harbor on 7 December and conquers large parts of Southeast Asia and the Pacific. From 1942, after Midway and Guadalcanal, Japan is forced onto the defensive.

mapNote.en: The map shows the largest area in 1943–1944, about 7.0 million km²; the source gives 7.4 million km² in 1942.

text.en: The emperor announces the surrender on the radio on 15 August, and it is signed on 2 September. Japan's rule in Korea ends.

mapNote.en: The map ends in 1945; the source counts the empire to 1947.

The source gives 3 January 1868–3 May 1947. The map shows the empire 1868–1945. Cliopatria does not distinguish between Japan and the colonies; the main country with the star is Japan's main islands and the Ryukyu Islands, delimited by hand from Cliopatria's area.

summary.en: The Ethiopian Empire, also called Abyssinia, comprised present-day Ethiopia and Eritrea. It was founded by the Solomonic dynasty around 1270 and lasted until the military coup in 1974. During the colonial era it was one of only two African countries that remained independent, together with Liberia.

text.en: Yekuno Amlak, who claimed descent from Aksum's last king and from King Solomon, took power from the Zagwe dynasty around 1270. The empire grew under Amda Seyon I (1314–1344) and Dawit I (1382–1413) and was at its strongest under Zara Yaqob (1434–1468).

The famine in Wollo in 1973, discontent in the cities and high fuel prices led to revolt in 1974. The military council, the Derg, deposed Emperor Haile Selassie on 12 September 1974, and the monarchy was abolished in March 1975.
No fixed capital in 1270–1635: the emperors travelled around with the court and lived in fortified camps. Then Gondar (1635–1855), Debre Tabor, Mekelle and from 1889 Addis Ababa.

Italy declared war in 1895, was defeated at Adwa in 1896 and had to recognise Ethiopia's independence. Italy attacked again in 1935, used mustard gas and occupied the country in 1936–1941. With British help Haile Selassie returned to the throne on 5 May 1941.
Menelik II conquered peoples and kingdoms in the west, south and east, among them Kaffa, Welayta and Harar. By 1898 the empire had largely acquired Ethiopia's present borders.

Haile Selassie abolished the legal basis of slavery in 1942. Ethiopia took part in founding the UN, and the Organisation of African Unity was formed in 1963 with its headquarters in Addis Ababa. The area was 1,221,900 km² in 1954.

The Lion of Judah. It was a title for the emperors of the Solomonic house, who traced their descent from King Solomon, and a map from 1683 by Hiob Ludolf describes the lion as the Ethiopian empire's royal emblem. The map shows the imperial flag with the lion in 1914–1935 and 1942–1974; between those periods and before 1914 it uses the lion as an emblem. On Haile Selassie's imperial banner the lion carries a staff with a cross; the simplified flag keeps only the flag's main motif.
Yekuno Amlak defeats the Zagwe king and takes the throne, with the support of the Orthodox Church.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1272.

text.en: Imam Ahmed Gran of the Adal Sultanate attacks with Ottoman support and is defeated only in 1543, with Portuguese help. The weakened empire loses large parts in the south.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire much smaller in 1534–1546.

text.en: Emperor Fasilides makes Gondar the permanent capital, a flourishing trading centre with palaces and churches. The source gives 1636 in the text and 1635 in the fact box.
Tewodros II ends the Zemene Mesafint, a time of fragmentation since 1769, and unites the empire again. He dies in 1868 during a British punitive expedition.
Ethiopia defeats Italy at Adwa. In the Treaty of Addis Ababa Italy has to recognise Ethiopia's independence. At the same time Menelik II conquers large areas in the south and east.

mapNote.en: The map shows Menelik's conquests in 1890–1908, when the area grows from about 0.24 to 1.13 million km².

text.en: Italy takes Addis Ababa on 5 May 1936 and merges Ethiopia with Eritrea and Italian Somaliland into Italian East Africa. Haile Selassie goes into exile and appeals to the League of Nations. He returns on 5 May 1941.

mapNote.en: The map lacks Ethiopia in 1936–1941.

text.en: After a UN decision Eritrea is federated with Ethiopia on 11 September 1952.

mapNote.en: The map shows Eritrea from 1953.

text.en: The military council, the Derg, deposes Haile Selassie on 12 September, and the monarchy is abolished in March 1975.

mapNote.en: The source gives around 1270–1974. The map shows the empire 1272–1935 and 1942–1974. After 1941 the map is based on Cliopatria's entry for Ethiopia, which here ends in 1974.

summary.en: The Soviet Union was a communist federal state in Europe and Asia in 1922–1991, ruled by the Communist Party. It was the world's largest country by area and one of the two superpowers during the Cold War.

text.en: The roots lay in the October Revolution of 1917, when the Bolsheviks under Lenin took power and formed the Russian SFSR. After the civil war Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and Transcaucasia were merged into the Soviet Union in December 1922.

Gorbachev's reforms in the 1980s were followed by national movements in the republics. After a failed coup attempt in August 1991 Russia, Ukraine and Belarus left the union, and on 26 December 1991 the dissolution was recognised. All fifteen republics became independent states.
Moscow.

Under Stalin forced collectivisation led to a famine in the 1930s that killed millions. The Gulag camp system was expanded, and the Great Terror at the end of the 1930s meant deportations, executions and show trials. Soviet troops later put down uprisings in East Germany, Hungary and Czechoslovakia.

The Soviet Union concluded a non-aggression pact with Nazi Germany in 1939 and invaded Poland in September. Germany attacked in 1941. With about 27 million dead the Soviet Union suffered worst of all countries. After the war the countries the Red Army had occupied were made into satellite states.
22,402,200 km², a sixth of the Earth's land area.

The hammer and sickle, a symbol of labour and the unity of workers, came into being in 1918 during the revolution. It was the centre of the Soviet Union's coat of arms, adopted in 1923 and used until the state was dissolved in 1991, and was also on the flag.
The Russian SFSR and the other Soviet republics join together in the Soviet Union in December. Lenin dies in 1924, and Stalin takes power after a power struggle.
Stalin abandons the NEP and introduces a planned economy and forced collectivisation of agriculture. The country industrialises rapidly, but the famine of the 1930s kills millions.
Through the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact the Soviet Union gains control of large parts of Eastern Europe. Germany attacks Poland in September, and the Soviet Union invades later the same month.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area growing only in 1940.

text.en: Germany attacks the Soviet Union in the largest land invasion in history, and the Eastern Front opens. The Soviet Union plays a decisive role when the Axis powers are defeated.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area decreasing in 1942–1944 and growing again in 1945.

text.en: The Soviet Union emerges from the war as a superpower and makes the occupied countries in Central and Eastern Europe into satellite states. The Warsaw Pact is formed in 1955.
The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1, the first satellite, and on 12 April 1961 Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space.
After the coup attempt in August, Russia, Ukraine and Belarus leave the union. Gorbachev recognises the dissolution on 26 December, and fifteen independent states take over.

mapNote.en: The source and the map give the same years, 1922–1991.

summary.en: The Kalmar Union was a personal union in the Nordic countries in 1397–1523. Denmark, Sweden (with large parts of present-day Finland) and Norway with the islands in the North Atlantic had the same king but kept their own laws and their own government. The union did not hold together the whole time, and in Sweden it was often only a name from the middle of the 15th century.

text.en: Queen Margaret of Denmark was behind the union. Her adopted son Eric of Pomerania was elected king in Denmark and Sweden in 1396 and crowned in Kalmar on 17 June 1397. An important reason was to hold back the power of the North German Hanseatic League around the Baltic Sea.

Gustav Vasa was elected king of Sweden on 6 June 1523 and marched into Stockholm eleven days later. Sweden then left the union for good. Frederick I renounced his claims to Sweden at Malmö in 1524. Denmark and Norway continued together as Denmark-Norway.
None by law. Wikipedia gives Copenhagen as the capital in practice, but without a source.

The Swedish nobility was dissatisfied that Denmark and Holstein dominated. The Engelbrekt rebellion, which began in 1434, led to King Eric being deposed. After 1448 the countries often had different kings, and Sweden was for a long time governed by regents.
Medieval Danish, Swedish and Norwegian as well as Latin were used officially. In addition, among others, Icelandic, Faroese, Finnish, Sámi and Low German were spoken.
No emblem. The source gives no coat of arms for the union, only that Eric of Pomerania was elected king under the banner of the House of the Griffin.
Eric of Pomerania is crowned in Kalmar on 17 June 1397. The three kingdoms now have the same king.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1402.

text.en: A rebellion in Sweden begins in 1434. It leads to King Eric being deposed in Denmark and Sweden in 1439 and in Norway in 1442.

Christian II enters Sweden with a large army. Sten Sture the Younger is killed at the Battle of Bogesund, Christian is crowned king of Sweden, and Sture's supporters are executed in large numbers in the Stockholm Bloodbath in November.

mapNote.en: The map does not count Sweden as part of the union in 1502–1520, when regents ruled, and shows it again in 1521–1525.

text.en: Gustav Vasa, who has led the revolt against Christian II from Dalarna with the support of Lübeck, is elected king of Sweden on 6 June 1523.

mapNote.en: The map shows the union up to and including 1525.
The sources give 1397–1523. The map shows the union 1402–1525.

summary.en: Prussia was a German state on the North European Plain from 1525 to 1947. It began as a duchy around Königsberg, was united with Brandenburg and in 1701 became a kingdom with Berlin as its capital. The House of Hohenzollern ruled for centuries, and in 1871 Prussia united the German states into the German Empire.

text.en: In 1525 the Teutonic Order's part of Prussia was made a secular duchy, which was subject to the Polish crown until 1657. The duchy was united with Brandenburg in 1618, and on 18 January 1701 Prussia became a kingdom.

The monarchy fell in the German Revolution of 1918, and Prussia became a free state in the Weimar Republic. The coup of 1932 and the Nazis' laws of 1934–1935 emptied it of power. The Allies formally dissolved Prussia on 25 February 1947. The land east of the Oder–Neisse had by then gone to Poland and the Soviet Union, and the rest was divided among German states.
Königsberg (1525–1701), then Berlin.

10.3 million inhabitants in 1816 and 24.7 million in 1871, then 60 per cent of the German Empire's population. In the German Empire Prussia had three fifths of the area and two thirds of the inhabitants.

The Prussian eagle, a black eagle. Emperor Frederick II gave the Teutonic Order the right to bear the empire's black eagle in 1229, and it remained the arms of the Prussian states until 1947. From 1701 the eagle wore a royal crown.
The Teutonic Order's land in Prussia becomes a secular duchy under Polish suzerainty.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1526.

text.en: The duchy and Brandenburg get the same prince on 27 August 1618. The lands are not yet connected.

mapNote.en: The map shows Brandenburg-Prussia from 1619.

text.en: Prussia becomes a kingdom on 18 January 1701, with Berlin as its capital. Shortly afterwards the country is counted among Europe's great powers.

mapNote.en: The map shows the kingdom from 1702.

text.en: Frederick the Great takes part in the first partition of Poland together with Austria and Russia. Brandenburg and Prussia are now connected.
Prussia unites the German states into the German Empire. Prussia remains as a state and dominates the empire.

mapNote.en: The map has no border of its own for Prussia after 1806; the country is part of the German Empire.

text.en: The Allied Control Council dissolves Prussia by Law No. 46, on 25 February 1947.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1525–1947. The map shows Prussia 1526–1806: the duchy (1526–1618), Brandenburg-Prussia (1619–1701) and the kingdom (1702–1806). From 1807 Cliopatria has no border of its own for Prussia: the country is counted as part of the French Empire and the Confederation of the Rhine, then of the German Confederation (1815–1867), the North German Confederation (1868–1870) and the German Empire. Some very small Prussian areas that Cliopatria shows in 1807–1863 are not included.

summary.en: Yugoslavia, “the land of the South Slavs”, was a country in the Balkans in 1918–1992 and the first state of their own for the South Slavic peoples. It began as a kingdom and after the Second World War became a communist federal republic with six constituent republics.

text.en: The country was formed on 1 December 1918, when the Kingdom of Serbia joined the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, which had been formed on Austria-Hungary's South Slavic territories. It was first called the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and from 3 October 1929 the Kingdom of Yugoslavia.

After Tito's death in 1980 and crises during the 1980s Slovenia and Croatia declared independence on 25 June 1991. By April 1992 four of the six republics had left the country. On 27 April 1992 the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro) was adopted, and the break-up was formally complete. The Yugoslav Wars followed, 1991–2001.
Belgrade.

label.en: The Second World War and Tito

text.en: The Axis powers invaded the country on 6 April 1941. The Partisans under Josip Broz Tito received the Allies' support, and on 29 November 1945 Yugoslavia became a federal republic without a king. Tito ruled from 1944 until his death in 1980.
Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia and Slovenia. In Serbia there were also the autonomous provinces of Vojvodina and Kosovo.
17.5 million inhabitants in 1955 and 23.5 million in 1991, according to Yugoslavia's statistical yearbooks.

The emblem of Socialist Yugoslavia: six torches burning in a common flame, one for each constituent republic. The emblem was drawn in 1943 and had five torches until 1963. The Kingdom of Yugoslavia (1918–1941) instead had a white double-headed eagle, developed from Serbia's coat of arms, and is shown with it.
Serbia joins the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs on 1 December 1918. The kingdom gains international recognition in 1922.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1919.

text.en: The country changes its name to the Kingdom of Yugoslavia on 3 October 1929, under King Alexander I's dictatorship.
The Axis powers invade and occupy the country in April 1941. The Second World War in Yugoslavia begins.

mapNote.en: The map shows no Yugoslavia in 1941–1944.

text.en: The constituent assembly abolishes the monarchy on 29 November 1945. The country gets Istria, Rijeka and Zadar from Italy.
Slovenia and Croatia declare independence on 25 June 1991. The wars begin.

mapNote.en: The map ends in 1991.

text.en: On 27 April 1992 the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia is adopted, which consists only of Serbia and Montenegro.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1918–1992. The map shows the kingdom 1919–1940 and 1945 and the federal republic 1946–1991. During the occupation 1941–1944 Cliopatria counts the country as part of Nazi Germany.

summary.en: Czechoslovakia was a country in Central Europe in 1918–1992, with Prague as its capital. It was formed when Austria-Hungary fell apart and was peacefully divided into the Czech Republic and Slovakia at the new year of 1993.

text.en: The country declared itself independent on 28 October 1918, when Austria-Hungary fell apart. Tomáš Masaryk and Edvard Beneš led the work and became the first presidents. The Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye confirmed the independence.

After the Velvet Revolution in 1989 the country was divided into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, without violence. The division took effect from 31 December 1992 and is called the Velvet Divorce. No referendum was held, and the division was unpopular when it was made.
Prague. The area was 127,906 km².

After the Munich Agreement in 1938 Nazi Germany took the Sudetenland, and in March 1939 the rest was broken up: Bohemia-Moravia became a German protectorate, Slovakia a state of its own and Carpathian Ukraine went to Hungary. The country was re-established in 1945, but Carpathian Ukraine became part of the Soviet Union.
The Communist Party took power in a coup on 25 February 1948. The Prague Spring of 1968 was crushed when the Soviet Union and other countries in the Warsaw Pact invaded the country on 21 August 1968.
The Bohemian lion, the standing lion with a double tail. The small coat of arms from 1920 was Bohemia's arms with Slovakia's arms on top, and after 1945 it was the arms most used.
Czechoslovakia is proclaimed on 28 October 1918.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1919.

text.en: The Munich Agreement of 30 September 1938 gives the Sudetenland to Nazi Germany.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area decreasing from about 145,000 to 86,000 km² in 1938.

text.en: On 14 March 1939 the country is divided. The government-in-exile under Beneš is recognised by the Allies.

mapNote.en: The map shows no Czechoslovakia in 1939–1946; Cliopatria counts the country as part of Nazi Germany and in 1945–1946 as part of the Soviet Union.

text.en: The Communists take power on 25 February 1948, and the country becomes part of the Eastern Bloc.
The Warsaw Pact invades the country on 21 August 1968 and ends the Prague Spring.

mapNote.en: The map shows no Czechoslovakia in 1969–1990: Cliopatria counts the country as part of the Soviet Union, although according to the sources it remained as a state of its own.

text.en: Peaceful protests on 17–28 November 1989 force the Communist leaders out.
The country is divided into the Czech Republic and Slovakia. The division takes effect from 31 December 1992.

mapNote.en: The map ends in 1991.

The sources give 1918–1992. The map shows the country only in 1919–1938, 1947–1968 and 1991. Cliopatria counts the country as part of Nazi Germany in 1939–1944 and of the Soviet Union in 1945–1946 and 1969–1990.

summary.en: Gran Colombia, officially the Republic of Colombia, was a state in northern South America in 1819–1831. It comprised present-day Colombia, mainland Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela as well as parts of northern Peru and north-western Brazil.

text.en: The state was proclaimed in a fundamental law at the Congress of Angostura in 1819, during the war against Spain, but came into being in earnest only when the Congress of Cúcuta adopted a constitution in 1821.

The struggle between supporters of a strong central power around Simón Bolívar and supporters of a federation around Francisco de Paula Santander, and conflicts between the regions, split the state. Bolívar resigned in 1830, the union was dissolved at the end of the year and formally abolished in 1831. Venezuela, Ecuador and New Granada became states of their own.
Bogotá.
About 3,064,800 km² and 2.58 million inhabitants in 1825.

The coat of arms from 6 October 1821: two cornucopias with flowers and fruit around a bundle of spears and arrows, bound with a ribbon in the colours of the flag, as a sign of wealth, strength and unity. Before that other arms were used in 1819–1821.
The Congress of Angostura adopts the fundamental law for the Republic of Colombia.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1822.

text.en: The Congress of Cúcuta adopts a constitution on 30 August 1821. The state becomes a centrally governed unitary state.
José Antonio Páez defies the government, and Venezuela comes close to breaking away. Bolívar calms the situation with an amnesty in January 1827.
Bolívar declares war on Peru on 3 June 1828 over the territories of Jaén and Maynas. The war ends with the Treaty of Guayaquil in 1829.
Bolívar resigns, and the union is dissolved in the last months of the year. It is formally abolished in 1831.

mapNote.en: The map shows Gran Colombia up to and including 1833.
The sources give 1819–1831. The map shows the state 1822–1833.

summary.en: The Republic of Texas was an independent country in North America from 2 March 1836 to 19 February 1846, between Mexico and the United States. Mexico never recognised the independence and regarded Texas as a rebellious province.

text.en: The Texas Revolution broke out on 2 October 1835, after Mexico's President Santa Anna had abolished the states' self-government. On 2 March 1836 a convention at Washington-on-the-Brazos adopted a declaration of independence. The major fighting ended on 21 April 1836, and in the Treaties of Velasco the captured Santa Anna recognised the independence. Mexico's congress never approved the treaties.

The United States admitted Texas as the 28th state on 29 December 1845, and power was handed over on 19 February 1846. The United States inherited the border dispute with Mexico, and the annexation led to the Mexican–American War.
Five temporary capitals in 1836, among them Washington-on-the-Brazos, then Houston (1837–1839) and Austin (1839–1846).
About 135,000 inhabitants in 1845 (estimate). Mexico or the Comanche controlled or claimed large parts of the territory that the republic counted as its own.

The lone star. The republic's first flag had a gold star on blue, and in 1839 the Lone Star flag was adopted. The republic's seal from 25 January 1839 is the model for the state's seal, which has a five-pointed star.
The convention at Washington-on-the-Brazos declares Texas independent on 2 March 1836.
President Sam Houston moves the capital to the city of Houston.
The next president, Mirabeau B. Lamar, moves the capital to the new city of Austin.
Texas becomes the 28th state of the United States on 29 December 1845. Power is handed over on 19 February 1846.

mapNote.en: The map ends in 1845.
The sources give 1836–1846. The map shows the republic 1836–1845, with the same area throughout.

summary.en: The Kingdom of Hawaii was an island state in the Pacific in 1795–1893 that finally comprised all the inhabited Hawaiian Islands. It was ruled by the House of Kamehameha and from 1874 by the Kalākaua dynasty, until the monarchy was overthrown in 1893.

text.en: Kamehameha I conquered Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi in 1795 and united them under one rule. In 1810 Kauaʻi and Niʻihau joined voluntarily, and by then all the islands were united.

In 1887 King Kalākaua was forced to accept a new constitution under threat from an armed militia. When Queen Liliʻuokalani wanted to replace it she was overthrown on 17 January 1893 by the Committee of Safety, with the support of American marines. The Republic of Hawaii was proclaimed on 4 July 1894, and the United States annexed the islands in 1898.
Waikīkī, Honolulu and Kailua-Kona, depending on where Kamehameha I moved (1795–1820), then Lāhainā (1820–1845) and Honolulu (1845–1893).
About 250,000 inhabitants in 1800, 130,313 in 1832 and 89,990 in 1890. Diseases that Europeans and Americans brought with them caused the Indigenous population to decline rapidly.

A pūloʻuloʻu, a ball covered in kapa on a staff, which was carried in front of a chief as a sign of kapu (sacredness) and protection. It stands in two fields in the kingdom's coat of arms, adopted in 1845.
Kamehameha I conquers Oʻahu and unites most of the islands.
Kauaʻi and Niʻihau join the kingdom.
Hawaii becomes a constitutional monarchy on 8 October 1840.
Kalākaua is forced to accept a constitution that reduces the king's power.
The Committee of Safety deposes Liliʻuokalani on 17 January 1893 and installs a provisional government.

mapNote.en: The map shows the kingdom up to and including 1894.
Wikipedia gives 1795–1893, Wikidata 1795–1895. The map shows the kingdom 1791–1894; the first years are Kamehameha's realm before all the islands were united.

summary.en: Neutral Moresnet was a small area of 3.5 km² between present-day Belgium and Germany, which the neighbouring countries governed jointly in 1816–1920. It was 1.5 km wide and 2.5 km long.

text.en: After the Congress of Vienna the Netherlands and Prussia could not agree on who should get the Altenberg zinc mine (Vieille Montagne). At Aachen on 26 June 1816 the district of Moresnet was divided into three parts. The mine and the adjoining village became neutral until further notice and were governed jointly, and neither army was allowed to enter. Belgium took over the Netherlands' role in 1830.
Germany annexed the area during the First World War. The Treaty of Versailles gave it to Belgium, and from January 1920 it became the municipality of Kelmis.
Two royal commissioners, one from each neighbour, and a mayor whom they appointed. A municipal council was added in 1859, but the inhabitants had no right to vote.

The mining company Vieille Montagne was the largest employer and ran housing, shops, a hospital and a bank. The inhabitants increased from 256 in 1815 to 4,668 in 1914. The mine ran out in 1885. An attempt at stamps of its own in 1886 and a casino in 1903 were stopped, and in 1908 it was proposed that the area should become an Esperanto state, Amikejo.
No emblem. The source shows only a flag for the area, no coat of arms.
The Netherlands and Prussia divide Moresnet on 26 June 1816 and make the area around the zinc mine neutral.
When the zinc mine is exhausted it becomes uncertain whether the area can continue to exist.
The mine doctor Wilhelm Molly proposes that Neutral Moresnet should become the world's first state where Esperanto is spoken.
Germany annexes the area on 27 June 1915, during the First World War.
The Treaty of Versailles gives the area to Belgium, and on 10 January 1920 it becomes the municipality of Kelmis.

mapNote.en: Cliopatria has no border for Neutral Moresnet: the area is counted as part of the German Confederation and the German Empire and from 1919 of Belgium. It is too small for the map and is shown as a point at Kelmis, with coordinates from Wikipedia and Wikidata.

summary.en: The USA (the United States of America) is a federal republic in North America. The country declared its independence from Britain in 1776 and then grew westward through purchase, settlement and conquest of land that European powers and Indigenous peoples controlled.

text.en: The Thirteen Colonies declared independence in July 1776, in the midst of the War of Independence of 1775–1783. The Peace of Paris in 1783 gave the country international recognition and land westward to the Mississippi River.

The Articles of Confederation were in force in 1781–1789. The constitution of 1787 took effect in 1789 and made the country a federal republic with three branches of power. George Washington became the first president.
Eleven southern states seceded in 1861 and formed the Confederate States of America. The United States won the war in 1865, the country was united again and slavery was abolished.
Washington, D.C. The area is given as between 9,629,091 and 9,866,624 km², depending on how it is counted.
The Lee Resolution of 2 July 1776 declares the colonies independent, and the Declaration of Independence is adopted two days later.
Britain recognises the United States, which gets land westward to the Mississippi River, northward to present-day Canada and southward to Spanish Florida.
The purchase of Louisiana from France almost doubles the country's area. Spain cedes Florida in 1819.

mapNote.en: The map shows no doubling in 1803: the area grows in steps, from about 1.2 to 2.1 million km² in 1803–1823.

text.en: The United States annexes Texas in 1845 and gets Oregon in 1846. After the war of 1846–1848 Mexico recognises the United States' right to Texas, New Mexico and California.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area increasing from about 3.0 to 3.5 million km² in 1846.

text.en: Eleven southern states secede and form the Confederate States of America. The war lasts until 1865.

mapNote.en: The map shows the United States without the southern states in 1861–1865, and the area falls from about 4.2 to 2.5 million km² in 1861.

text.en: Alaska is bought from Russia.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area increasing to about 5.7 million km² in 1866 and 7.9 million km² in 1868.

title.en: Hawaii and the war against Spain

text.en: Hawaii is annexed. The same year Spain cedes Puerto Rico, the Philippines and Guam after losing the war against the United States.

mapNote.en: The map shows only a small increase in 1898.

text.en: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor, and the United States enters the Second World War on the Allied side.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area increasing to about 12 million km² in 1941–1945.

text.en: The Philippines become fully independent on 4 July 1946. Puerto Rico and Guam remain American territories.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1776 as the start, like the map. During the Civil War of 1861–1865 the map shows the southern states as a country of their own, the Confederate States of America.

summary.en: The Confederate States of America was a republic in the southern United States in 1861–1865. It was formed by states that seceded from the United States to protect slavery, and was never recognised as an independent state, either by other countries or by the United States.

text.en: Seven southern states formed the Confederacy on 8 February 1861, after Abraham Lincoln had been elected president. After the attack on Fort Sumter in April 1861 four more joined: Virginia, Arkansas, Tennessee and North Carolina.
Historians are largely agreed that slavery was the main reason for secession. The myth of the “Lost Cause”, which denies this, is rejected by scholarship.

After four years of war most of the Confederate forces had surrendered or stopped fighting by May 1865. The most important surrender was General Robert E. Lee's on 9 April 1865. The states were then readmitted to Congress, each after approving the Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution, which banned slavery.
Montgomery in Alabama from February to May 1861, then Richmond in Virginia.

The battle flag: a broad blue Saint Andrew's cross with a white border and white stars on a red field, a proposal for a national flag that was rejected and instead became the army's battle flag. It was never the Confederacy's national flag, but it was included in the two later national flags (1863–1865) and is today the South's best-known symbol. After the war it has been used amid political, cultural and racial controversies in the United States. The first national flag was the “Stars and Bars” (1861–1863).
Seven southern states form the Confederacy on 8 February 1861. After the attack on Fort Sumter in April four more join, and the capital is moved to Richmond.
The Confederate leadership introduces a central government in Richmond and the first draft, on 16 April 1862.
General Robert E. Lee surrenders on 9 April 1865, and by May most of the Confederate forces have given up.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1861–1865, like the map. The map shows the Confederate territory shrinking from about 1.7 million km² in 1861 to 1.1 million km² in 1865.

summary.en: Mexico is a federal republic in North America with Mexico City as its capital. The country became independent from Spain in 1821 and lost almost half its territory in the war against the United States in 1846–1848.

text.en: The priest Miguel Hidalgo began the war of independence in 1810 with the Grito de Dolores. The war lasted until 1821, when the last Spanish viceroy signed the Treaty of Córdoba on 24 August.

First an empire under Agustín I (1822–1823), then a federal republic from 1824. Santa Anna made the country centralised in 1835, which led to civil war and to, among other things, Texas declaring independence. In 1864–1867 the country was again an empire, under Maximilian of Habsburg and with the support of France.

The revolution of 1910–1920 began with a revolt against Porfirio Díaz after the electoral fraud of 1910. It produced the constitution of 1917, which is still in force. According to the source the war killed 900,000 of the country's 15 million inhabitants.
Mexico City, founded on the ruins of the Aztecs' Tenochtitlan. The area is 1,972,550 km².
The Treaty of Córdoba on 24 August 1821 ends the war of independence against Spain.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1822.

text.en: Agustín de Iturbide becomes Emperor Agustín I. He is overthrown as early as 1823, and Central America and Chiapas leave the union.
The First Mexican Republic is formed, with Guadalupe Victoria as its first president.
After Santa Anna has made the country centralised, civil war spreads, and Texas declares independence.

mapNote.en: In 1836–1847 the map shows both the federal republic and the centralist republic, in two shades of the same colour.

text.en: After the United States' invasion in 1846 Mexico loses a large part of its territory in the north.

mapNote.en: The map shows the country's area decreasing from about 2.8 to 2.1 million km² in 1848.

text.en: With French support Maximilian of Habsburg becomes emperor. The republic under Benito Juárez continues the struggle.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire only from 1865.

text.en: Maximilian is executed on 19 June 1867, and Juárez returns as president.
A revolt against Porfirio Díaz after the electoral fraud of 1910 begins a ten-year civil war.

mapNote.en: The map lacks Mexico in 1913–1919: Cliopatria shows no country there during the revolution.

text.en: The revolution's victors adopt the constitution of 1917, which is still in force.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1821 as the year of independence. The map shows the country from 1822 and divides it by form of government: the First Mexican Empire 1822–1823, the federal republic 1824–1865, the centralist republic 1836–1847, the Second Mexican Empire 1865–1867 and Mexico from 1868. The map lacks Mexico in 1913–1919.

summary.en: Brazil is South America's largest country, with Brasília as its capital. The country became independent from Portugal in 1822 as an empire and became a republic in 1889.

text.en: Brazil was a Portuguese colony and from 1815 a united kingdom with Portugal, after the Portuguese court had moved to Rio de Janeiro. Prince Pedro declared the country independent on 7 September 1822 and was proclaimed Emperor Pedro I a month later.

The constitution of 1824 gave the country a two-chamber parliament and freedom of religion and the press. Slavery was abolished in stages and completely in May 1888. On 15 November 1889 the monarchy was overthrown in a military coup.

The revolution of 1930 brought Getúlio Vargas to power, and his coup in 1937 began the authoritarian Estado Novo. Democracy returned in 1945. A military dictatorship ruled in 1964–1985, and the present constitution dates from 1988.
Rio de Janeiro, and from 1960 the newly built city of Brasília.
Prince Pedro declares Brazil independent on 7 September 1822 and becomes Emperor Pedro I.
The war against the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata ends with the province of Cisplatina becoming the independent republic of Uruguay.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area decreasing from about 8.0 to 7.8 million km² in 1828.

text.en: The empire goes to war against Paraguay, from 1865 in the Triple Alliance with Argentina and Uruguay. The war lasts until 1870.
The Golden Law abolishes slavery in May 1888.
The monarchy is overthrown in a military coup on 15 November 1889.
The revolution of 1930 brings Getúlio Vargas to power. From 1937 he rules as a dictator in the Estado Novo, until 1945.
The new capital Brasília is inaugurated.
The military takes power with support from the United States and rules until 1985.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1822 as the year of independence, like the map. Cliopatria divides the republic into four entries by form of government (1890–1931 and 1946–1966, 1932–1945, 1967–1986 and from 1987); here they are shown as one.

summary.en: Argentina is a federal state in southern South America with Buenos Aires as its capital. The country emerged from the Spanish Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata and declared independence on 9 July 1816.

text.en: The May Revolution of 1810 replaced the viceroy with a junta in Buenos Aires. The Congress of Tucumán declared the country independent on 9 July 1816. A long civil war between centralists and federalists followed, lasting until 1880.

The name Argentine Republic appears for the first time in the constitution of 1826. The Argentine Confederation was laid down in the constitution of 1853, and in 1860 the name was fixed as the Argentine Republic.

The coup of 1930 was followed by more in 1943, 1955, 1962, 1966 and 1976. The military junta after 1976 persecuted and murdered thousands of critics in the Dirty War, which lasted until the election of Raúl Alfonsín in 1983.
Buenos Aires. The area is 2,780,085 km².
The Congress of Tucumán declares the country independent on 9 July 1816.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1834.

text.en: After the fall of Juan Manuel de Rosas in 1852 a liberal federal constitution is adopted.
Bartolomé Mitre defeats Urquiza at Pavón and becomes the first president of the united country.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area increasing from about 1.4 to 1.6 million km² in 1861.

text.en: Argentina declares war on Paraguay and concludes the Triple Alliance with Brazil and Uruguay.
Military campaigns in 1878–1884 against the Indigenous peoples of the Pampas and Patagonia take their land.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area increasing from about 1.7 to 2.0 million km² in 1880 and 2.8 million km² in 1885.

text.en: The military overthrows Isabel Perón. The junta persecutes and murders thousands of critics until 1983.
Argentina invades the Falkland Islands on 2 April 1982. The forces surrender on 14 June, and the military leadership resigns.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1816 as the year of independence. The map shows the country from 1834 and calls it the Argentine Confederation all the way to 1929, although the name Argentine Republic was fixed in 1860; here it is called Argentina throughout.

summary.en: Paraguay is a landlocked republic in South America with Asunción as its capital. The country counts its independence from Spain from 1811.

text.en: Paraguay overthrew the Spanish administration on 14 May 1811. José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia ruled as dictator in 1814–1840 and kept the country almost isolated. Carlos Antonio López declared the country officially independent in 1842.

label.en: The War of the Triple Alliance

text.en: The war against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay in 1864–1870 became a catastrophe. At least half the population died, and the country lost 25–33 per cent of its territory to Argentina and Brazil. Argentine and Brazilian troops occupied the country until 1876.
In the Chaco War against Bolivia in 1932–1935 Paraguay won most of the disputed Chaco area.
Alfredo Stroessner ruled in 1954–1989 and was overthrown in a military coup, which began the present democratic era.
Asunción, founded in 1537.
Paraguay overthrows the Spanish administration on 14 May 1811.

title.en: The War of the Triple Alliance

text.en: The war begins at the end of 1864, at first against Brazil. Argentina and Uruguay enter in 1865.
President Francisco Solano López is killed at Cerro Corá on 1 March 1870. The country is occupied until 1876.

mapNote.en: The map shows a very small Paraguay in 1868–1869 and lacks the country in 1870–1876.

text.en: Paraguay defeats Bolivia and wins most of the Chaco.

mapNote.en: The map shows the area increasing from about 159,000 to 402,000 km² in 1936.

text.en: Alfredo Stroessner takes power and rules as a dictator for 35 years.
Stroessner is overthrown in a military coup, and the present democratic era begins.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1811 as the start, like the map. The map shows a very small Paraguay in 1868–1869, lacks the country in 1870–1876 and shows a smaller country in 1877–1935 (about 159,000 km²) than from 1936 (about 402,000 km²).

summary.en: Uruguay, officially the Oriental Republic of Uruguay, is a republic in south-eastern South America with Montevideo as its capital. The country became independent in 1828, after a struggle between Portugal, Spain, the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata and Brazil.

text.en: Portuguese troops took Montevideo in 1817, and the area became the province of Cisplatina. On 25 August 1825 the 33 Orientals under Juan Antonio Lavalleja declared independence, which led to the Cisplatine War. The Treaty of Montevideo in 1828 made Uruguay an independent state, and the first constitution was adopted on 18 July 1830.
The Great War between the Colorados and the Blancos lasted for 13 years from 1839 and drew in Argentina, Brazil, Britain and France. Montevideo was besieged from 1843.
The military dissolved parliament in 1973 and ruled until 1985.
Montevideo. The area is about 176,215 km².
Juan Antonio Lavalleja and the 33 Orientals declare independence on 25 August 1825.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1828.

text.en: The treaty makes Uruguay an independent state.
The civil war between the Colorados and the Blancos begins and lasts for 13 years.
Uruguay concludes the Triple Alliance with Brazil and Argentina against Paraguay.
The military dissolves parliament and rules until 1985.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1828 as the year of independence, like the map. The border is almost the same throughout.

summary.en: Israel is a parliamentary republic on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean. The state was proclaimed on 14 May 1948, when the British Mandate for Palestine ended, and the day after the neighbouring countries' armies attacked.

text.en: Israel was proclaimed on 14 May 1948, when the British Mandate for Palestine ended. The armistice of 1949 left the country with a larger area than the UN partition plan had given it.
A parliamentary republic. The parliament, the Knesset, is elected proportionally, and the president has mainly ceremonial duties.

In the Six-Day War in 1967 Israel occupied the West Bank, Gaza and Egypt's Sinai Peninsula, and the country then annexed East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights. Peace was made with Egypt in 1979, and Sinai was returned in 1982. Peace with Jordan followed in 1994.

Jerusalem is the seat of government and the proclaimed capital, but its status is disputed and has limited international recognition. The area is given as 20,770 or 22,072 km², depending on the source.
David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel on 14 May 1948 in Tel Aviv. The next morning armies from Egypt, Transjordan, Syria and Iraq enter Palestine.
Israel concludes an armistice with Egypt on 24 February 1949 and later the same year with Lebanon, Transjordan and Syria.
Israel conquers and occupies the Sinai Peninsula, the Gaza Strip, the West Bank with East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights on 5–10 June 1967.

mapNote.en: The map counts Sinai as part of Israel from 1967, like Cliopatria. The West Bank with East Jerusalem, Gaza and the Golan Heights are not counted as part of Israel, because the map follows Sweden's position according to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD) (checked 2026-11-06).

text.en: Egypt and Syria attack on 6 October 1973, on the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur. The fighting ends on 25 October.

mapNote.en: The map shows Sinai outside Israel in 1973–1975 and again inside Israel in 1976–1982.

text.en: Israel and Egypt make peace in 1979, and Sinai is returned to Egypt in 1982.
The Oslo Accords give the Palestinians limited self-government in the West Bank and Gaza.
Israel and Jordan make peace in 1994.

mapNote.en: The border is disputed. The map follows Cliopatria, except in present-day disputed borders, where it follows Sweden's official position according to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD) (checked 2026-11-06): the West Bank with East Jerusalem, Gaza and the Golan Heights are not counted as part of Israel from 1967, because Sweden sees them as occupied territories outside Israel within the 1967 borders. The borders of those areas come from Natural Earth; Cliopatria counts them as part of Israel. Sinai (1956–1957, 1967–1972 and 1976–1982), Gaza in 1956–1957 and southern Lebanon in 1983–1986 are shown as in Cliopatria. The sources describe the West Bank, Gaza and Sinai as occupied territories.

summary.en: According to Sweden's position the State of Palestine consists of the West Bank with East Jerusalem and Gaza, areas that Israel occupied in 1967. Sweden recognised the State of Palestine on 30 October 2014.

text.en: Sweden recognised the State of Palestine on 30 October 2014. Sweden's Consulate General in Jerusalem, with seconded staff since 1991, handles the official contacts with the Palestinian Authority.

According to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD) the EU's agreements with Israel apply to the State of Israel within the 1967 borders and not to the West Bank, East Jerusalem, Gaza or the Golan Heights, which are counted as occupied territories. The EU and Sweden hold that the Israeli settlements in the West Bank and East Jerusalem are contrary to international law.

mapNote.en: The border is disputed. Cliopatria has no Palestinian state after 1948 and counts the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza as part of Israel from 1967. The map follows Sweden's official position according to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD) (checked 2026-11-06) and shows the State of Palestine from Sweden's recognition in 2014, with borders from Natural Earth. The map says nothing about who controls the areas; Israel occupies them according to UD. Before 2014 the areas are shown without a state.

summary.en: Egypt became an independent kingdom in 1922, when Britain unilaterally declared the country independent, and a republic in 1953. The capital is Cairo. Ancient Egypt exists as a separate empire on the map.

text.en: Britain declared Egypt independent in February 1922, and Fuad I became king on 15 March the same year. Wikipedia gives both 22 and 28 February for the declaration; Wikidata gives 28 February.
Fuad I reigned in 1922–1936 and Farouk I in 1936–1952. A treaty with Britain in 1936 forced the British to withdraw their troops from Egypt, except from the Suez Canal Zone.
Free Officers under Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser overthrew King Farouk on 22–23 July 1952, and Egypt was proclaimed a republic on 18 June 1953. Nasser became president in 1956.
Cairo. The area is 1,010,408 km².
Britain declares Egypt independent in February 1922, and Fuad I becomes king.
The Free Officers overthrow King Farouk on 22–23 July 1952. Egypt becomes a republic on 18 June 1953.
Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal on 26 July 1956. Israel enters Sinai with the support of France and Britain.

mapNote.en: The map counts Sinai as part of Israel in 1956–1957.

text.en: Egypt and Syria join together on 22 February 1958. The union ends after a coup in Syria on 28 September 1961.

mapNote.en: The map counts Syria as part of the United Arab Republic until 1966 and in 1961–1966 also shows Syria as a country of its own.

text.en: Israel conquers the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip.
Egyptian forces cross the Suez Canal on 6 October 1973 and knock out Israel's fortifications along the canal.
Egypt signs the Camp David Accords in 1978 and recognises Israel. Sinai is returned completely to Egypt in 1982.

mapNote.en: The map counts Sinai as part of Egypt in 1973–1975, as part of Israel in 1976–1982 and then again as part of Egypt.

text.en: Hosni Mubarak is overthrown in the revolution of 2011.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1922, like the sources. It follows Cliopatria's names: the United Arab Republic 1958–1972 and the Arab Republic of Egypt from 1973.

summary.en: Syria is a republic in the Middle East with Damascus as its capital. The country became independent from France after the Second World War. The Baath Party took power in 1963, and the Assad regime, which came to power in 1970, fell in December 2024.

text.en: Syria was a French mandate after the First World War. The country became independent on paper in 1945, when it joined the UN, and in practice when the French troops left the country in April 1946.
Syria joined Egypt on 22 February 1958. The union ended after a coup in Syria on 28 September 1961.
The Baath Party's military committee took power in a coup on 8 March 1963 and made Syria a one-party state. Through a new coup in 1970 Hafez al-Assad came to power.
The protests of 2011 grew into a civil war that lasted for 13 years. The Assad regime fell on 8 December 2024, and the country has since been governed by a transitional government.
Damascus. The area is 185,180 km².
The French troops leave Syria in April 1946, and the country becomes independent in practice.

mapNote.en: The map shows Syria as a country of its own only from 1946. During the mandate period Cliopatria shows the country as a French mandate.

text.en: Syria and Egypt form the United Arab Republic on 22 February 1958. Syria breaks out on 28 September 1961.

mapNote.en: The map counts Syria as part of the United Arab Republic in 1958–1966 and in 1961–1966 also shows Syria as a country of its own.

text.en: The Baath Party's military committee takes power on 8 March 1963.
Israel conquers the Golan Heights in the last two days of the Six-Day War, 9–10 June 1967.

mapNote.en: The Golan Heights are not counted as part of Israel from 1967, because the map follows Sweden's position that they are occupied (UD, checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria does not count them as part of Syria, so the area is empty on the map.

text.en: Syria attacks on the Golan Heights on 6 October 1973, at the same time as Egypt crosses the Suez Canal.
The protests of 2011 grow into a civil war.

mapNote.en: The map shows a smaller area from 2014, about 119,000 km² compared with 186,000 km² before.

text.en: The Assad regime falls on 8 December 2024.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1946. Cliopatria counts Syria as part of the United Arab Republic in 1958–1966, so the country is missing as a country of its own in 1958–1960 and appears twice in 1961–1966.

summary.en: Jordan is a kingdom in the Middle East with Amman as its capital. It began as the Emirate of Transjordan under British protection in 1921 and became an independent kingdom in 1946.

text.en: The Emirate of Transjordan was formed on 11 April 1921 with Abdullah as emir and became a British protectorate. On 25 May 1946 the country became an independent kingdom with Abdullah as its first king.
A semi-constitutional monarchy where the king has great power over both government and legislation.

Jordan took control of the West Bank in the war of 1948 and annexed it on 24 April 1950. Israel occupied the area in the Six-Day War in 1967. In 1988 Jordan renounced its claims in favour of the Palestinians and the PLO.
Amman. The area is 89,342 km².
The Emirate of Transjordan is formed on 11 April 1921 with Abdullah as emir.
Transjordan becomes an independent kingdom on 25 May 1946.

mapNote.en: The map shows the country only from 1947. Before that Cliopatria counts it as part of the British Empire.

text.en: Jordan annexes the West Bank on 24 April 1950.

mapNote.en: The map counts the West Bank as part of Jordan already from 1949.

text.en: Israel occupies the West Bank and East Jerusalem.

title.en: The claims to the West Bank

text.en: Jordan renounces its claims to the West Bank in favour of the Palestinians and the PLO.
Jordan and Israel make peace in 1994.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1947 and lacks Jordan in 1958–1959, when Cliopatria instead shows a federation between Iraq and Jordan.

summary.en: Iraq is a federal republic on the Euphrates and Tigris with Baghdad as its capital. The country became a kingdom under a British mandate in 1921, independent in 1932 and a republic in 1958.

text.en: Britain received a mandate over Mesopotamia in 1920 and on 23 August 1921 put Faisal I on the throne of the new Kingdom of Iraq. The country became independent on 3 October 1932 and joined the League of Nations.

A coup under Abd al-Karim Qasim overthrew the monarchy on 14 July 1958. The Baath Party took power in a coup in February 1963 and again on 17 July 1968. Saddam Hussein became president on 16 July 1979.

Iraq attacked Iran in 1980, and the war ended in a stalemate in 1988. On 2 August 1990 Iraq invaded and annexed Kuwait, which led to the Gulf War. A US-led coalition invaded Iraq in 2003 and overthrew the government.
Baghdad. The area is 438,317 km².
Britain puts Faisal I on the throne on 23 August 1921.
Iraq becomes independent on 3 October 1932.

mapNote.en: The map shows Iraq only from 1932, and in 1943–1946 Cliopatria counts the country as part of the British Empire.

text.en: Abd al-Karim Qasim's coup overthrows the monarchy on 14 July 1958.

mapNote.en: The map lacks Iraq in 1958–1959, when Cliopatria instead shows a federation between Iraq and Jordan.

text.en: Iraq attacks Iran in September 1980. The war ends in 1988.
Iraq invades and annexes Kuwait on 2 August 1990.

mapNote.en: The map counts Kuwait as part of Iraq in 1990.

text.en: A US-led coalition invades and occupies Iraq and overthrows the government. The Iraq War ends in 2011.

mapNote.en: The map lacks Iraq in 2006–2013, when Cliopatria counts the country as part of the United States, and shows the United States on top of Iraq from 2014.
The map begins in 1932, when Iraq became independent. It lacks Iraq in 1943–1946, 1958–1959 and 2006–2013, when Cliopatria counts the country as part of other empires.

summary.en: Iran, long called Persia in the West, is an Islamic republic with Tehran as its capital. The map shows the country from the Qajar dynasty in the late 18th century, through the Pahlavi dynasty 1925–1979, to the Islamic republic.

text.en: The Qajar dynasty took power from 1789, and Agha Mohammad Khan was crowned shah in 1796 and made Tehran his capital. After wars against Russia Iran had to cede most of its territories in the Caucasus in 1813 and the rest in 1828.
The revolution gave the country an elected parliament, the majlis, which met for the first time in 1906.

The parliament deposed the Qajar dynasty in 1925 and proclaimed the prime minister Reza Khan shah. In 1935 he asked foreign governments to use the name Iran. British and Soviet troops invaded the country on 25 August 1941, and Reza Shah was forced to abdicate in favour of his son Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. A coup that British and American intelligence services were behind overthrew Prime Minister Mossadegh on 19 August 1953.

The monarchy fell on 11 February 1979, and the Islamic republic was proclaimed on 1 April 1979 with Ruhollah Khomeini as Supreme Leader. Iraq attacked the country in 1980, and the war lasted eight years.
Tehran. The area is 1,648,195 km².
The Qajars' leader Agha Mohammad Khan is crowned shah in 1796.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1788, a year before the sources' 1789.

text.en: By the Treaty of Turkmenchay in 1828 Iran recognises Russian suzerainty over the whole of the South Caucasus and Dagestan.
The Constitutional Revolution gives Iran an elected parliament, which meets for the first time in 1906.
The parliament deposes the Qajar dynasty, and Reza Khan becomes shah in December 1925.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Pahlavi dynasty already from 1924.

text.en: British and Soviet troops invade Iran on 25 August 1941. Reza Shah abdicates, and his son Mohammad Reza Pahlavi becomes shah.

mapNote.en: The map shows a smaller Iran in 1942–1946, when Cliopatria counts the occupied parts as part of the British Empire and the Soviet Union.

text.en: A coup that British and American intelligence services were behind overthrows Prime Minister Mossadegh on 19 August 1953.
The monarchy falls on 11 February 1979, and the Islamic republic is proclaimed on 1 April 1979.
Iraq attacks Iran in September 1980. The war ends with a ceasefire in August 1988.

mapNote.en: The map begins in 1788 with the Qajar dynasty. Earlier Persian empires exist as empires of their own on the map, for example the Safavid Empire.

summary.en: Kuwait is an emirate on the Persian Gulf with Kuwait City as its capital. The al-Sabah family has ruled since the middle of the 18th century, and the country became independent from Britain in 1961.

text.en: The Bani Utbah settled in Kuwait some time in the middle of the 18th century. The selection of the Sabah family to rule is usually dated to 1752.
Sheikh Mubarak signed an agreement with the British in January 1899 that made Kuwait a British protectorate. Oil was found in the Burgan field on 22 February 1938.

Kuwait became independent on 19 June 1961. Iraq at first refused to recognise the country and claimed that it was part of Iraq. The British sent troops, and the Arab League then took over the protection of the border. In 1963 Iraq recognised Kuwait's border.
Iraq invaded Kuwait on 2 August 1990 and annexed the country on 8 August. The occupation ended at the end of February 1991; Wikipedia gives both 26 and 28 February.

label.en: Form of government, capital and area

text.en: An emirate where the emir is head of state. The constitution took effect on 11 November 1962, but the National Assembly has been suspended since 10 May 2024. The capital is Kuwait City, and the area is 17,818 km².
The Sabah family is chosen to rule Kuwait, according to the usual dating 1752.

mapNote.en: The map shows Kuwait 1757–1872 and then only from 1961.

text.en: Sheikh Mubarak signs an agreement in January 1899 that makes Kuwait a British protectorate.
Oil is found in the Burgan field on 22 February 1938.
Kuwait becomes independent on 19 June 1961.
Iraq invades Kuwait on 2 August 1990 and annexes the country on 8 August.

mapNote.en: The map counts Kuwait as part of Iraq in 1990.

text.en: The coalition's ground forces enter Kuwait on 24 February 1991, and the occupation ends a few days later.

mapNote.en: The map shows Kuwait 1757–1872 and from 1961, except 1990, when Cliopatria counts the country as part of Iraq. The sources date the Sabah family's rule to 1752, a few years before the map.

summary.en: India is a federal parliamentary republic in South Asia with New Delhi as its capital. The country became independent on 15 August 1947, when British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan, and became a republic in 1950.

text.en: British rule ended at midnight between 14 and 15 August 1947. British India was then divided into two states: India with a Hindu majority and Pakistan with a Muslim majority. The partition was followed by mass violence and large refugee flows.
A federal parliamentary republic. The constitution took effect on 26 January 1950. The country consists of 28 states and 8 union territories.

India and Pakistan fought over Kashmir in 1947–1948 and again in 1965. India fought a war against China in 1962 and in 1971 entered the Bangladesh Liberation War. Civil liberties were suspended in 1975–1977.
New Delhi. The area is 3,287,263 km².
British rule ends at midnight between 14 and 15 August 1947, and British India is divided into India and Pakistan. Jawaharlal Nehru becomes India's first prime minister.

mapNote.en: The map shows India from 1947, with a smaller area the first year.

text.en: India's constitution takes effect on 26 January 1950, and the country becomes a federal republic.
India invades and annexes the Portuguese colony of Goa in 1961.
India and China fight a short border war in 1962.
India enters the war in East Pakistan, which ends with Pakistan's surrender in Dhaka on 16 December 1971. East Pakistan becomes independent as Bangladesh.
India carries out its first nuclear test in 1974 and five more tests in 1998.
Civil liberties are suspended in 1975–1977.
From 1991 India opens its economy more, and the reforms tie the country closer to the world economy.

mapNote.en: The map shows India from 1947, like the sources. Before 1947 Cliopatria counts the area as part of British India (the British Raj) within the British Empire. The country's area on the map grows in 1948 and 1963. The border in Kashmir is disputed. The map shows Cliopatria's lines, that is who controls the areas and not whom they belong to: some are counted as part of India, some of Pakistan and some in the north-east of China. Sweden has no stated position on the border that we have found; UD writes about the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and about the Pakistan-controlled part of Kashmir (checked 2026-11-06).

summary.en: Pakistan is a federal parliamentary Islamic republic in South Asia with Islamabad as its capital. The country became independent on 14 August 1947, when British India was partitioned, and until 1971 also comprised East Pakistan, present-day Bangladesh.

text.en: Pakistan was formed on 14 August 1947 from the Muslim-majority areas of north-western and eastern British India. The country consisted of two parts far from each other, West Pakistan and East Pakistan.

A federal parliamentary Islamic republic. The constitution of 1956 made Pakistan an Islamic republic, and the present constitution dates from 1973. The country has alternated between civilian and military rule: the military took power in 1958, 1977 and 1999.
East Pakistan broke away after a nine-month war and became independent as Bangladesh, after Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971.
Islamabad. The capital was moved from Karachi to Islamabad during Ayub Khan's time as president. The area is 881,913 km².
British India is divided on 14–15 August 1947 into India and Pakistan. Pakistan then also comprises East Bengal, later East Pakistan.
The new constitution of 1956 makes Pakistan an Islamic republic.
President Iskander Mirza introduces martial law in October 1958 and abrogates the constitution. General Ayub Khan then takes over power.
Pakistan's army cracks down on the Bengali independence movement in March 1971. After India enters the war, Pakistan surrenders in Dhaka on 16 December, and East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh.

mapNote.en: The map counts East Pakistan as part of Pakistan up to and including 1972.

text.en: Under Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Pakistan gets a constitution in 1973 with a parliamentary form of government.
The constitution is suspended under Zia ul-Haq's martial law in 1977. It is reinstated with amendments in 1985.
Zia ul-Haq dies in a plane crash in 1988, and Benazir Bhutto is elected the country's first female prime minister.
Pakistan carries out six nuclear tests on 28 and 30 May 1998, in response to India's tests the same month.

mapNote.en: The map shows Pakistan from 1947, like the sources. Cliopatria counts East Pakistan as part of Pakistan up to and including 1972, and Bangladesh is shown as a country of its own only from 1973, although the sources give 1971. Before 1947 Cliopatria counts the area as part of British India (the British Raj). The border in Kashmir is disputed. The map shows Cliopatria's lines, that is who controls the areas and not whom they belong to: some are counted as part of India, some of Pakistan and some in the north-east of China. Sweden has no stated position on the border that we have found; UD writes about the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and about the Pakistan-controlled part of Kashmir (checked 2026-11-06).

summary.en: Bangladesh is a parliamentary republic in Bengal with Dhaka as its capital. The area was Pakistan's eastern part, East Pakistan, from 1947 and became independent after the Liberation War of 1971.

text.en: At the partition in 1947 the area became East Bengal, the most populous part of Pakistan. It was named East Pakistan in 1956. Independence was proclaimed on 26 March 1971, and the war ended with Pakistan's surrender on 16 December 1971.

The government of Pakistan cracked down hard on the Bengali Language Movement in 1952 and handled relief badly after the Bhola cyclone in 1970, when over 500,000 people died. In the election in December 1970 the Awami League won 167 of East Pakistan's 169 seats.

A parliamentary republic. The constitution was adopted on 4 November 1972; Wikipedia's fact box gives 16 December 1972 as the date of the present constitution. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman led the country until he was murdered in 1975. After military rule parliamentary democracy was reinstated in 1991.
Dhaka. Wikipedia gives the area as 148,460 km², Wikidata as 147,570 km².

title.en: East Bengal becomes part of Pakistan

text.en: At the partition of British India East Bengal becomes Pakistan's eastern and most populous part.

mapNote.en: The map counts the area as part of Pakistan in 1947–1972.

text.en: Pakistan's army cracks down on the Bengali movement on the night of 26 March 1971. The same day Sheikh Mujibur Rahman proclaims Bangladesh's independence.
After nine months of war, during which a genocide of Bengalis took place, Pakistan surrenders in Dhaka on 16 December 1971.

mapNote.en: The map shows Bangladesh only from 1973.

text.en: Bangladesh's constitution is adopted on 4 November 1972.
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, who has led the country since independence, is murdered in 1975.
The military dictator Hussain Muhammad Ershad is overthrown in a popular uprising in 1990, and parliamentary democracy is reinstated in 1991.
After an uprising against the authoritarian government Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is forced to resign and flee in August 2024.

mapNote.en: The map shows Bangladesh only from 1973. Cliopatria counts the area as part of Pakistan up to and including 1972, although independence was proclaimed in March 1971 and the war ended in December 1971.

summary.en: Afghanistan in Central Asia has its foundation in the Durrani Empire, which Ahmad Shah Durrani founded in 1747. Then came the emirate (from 1823), the kingdom (1926–1973) and the republic from 1973. The Taliban have ruled the country since 2021. The capital is Kabul.

text.en: After Nader Shah's death a tribal assembly (loya jirga) near Kandahar chose Ahmad Shah Durrani as shah in 1747. The empire had Kandahar as its capital and from 1776 Kabul. It took Mughal territories in 1749 and sacked Delhi in 1757. Kabul fell to the Barakzai clan in March 1823.

The emirate was founded in 1823 and from 1834 ruled by emirs, first Dost Mohammad Khan. The British tried to take the country in the First Anglo-Afghan War of 1838–1842 but withdrew. After the second war of 1878–1880 Britain took over the Afghan areas in present-day Pakistan. The country was a British protectorate until a treaty in 1919 gave it full independence; Wikipedia gives both 8 and 19 August 1919.

Amanullah Khan proclaimed himself king on 9 June 1926. He was overthrown in 1929, and Nadir Shah became king in October the same year. Zahir Shah reigned from 1933. The country was neutral in the Second World War, joined the UN in 1946 and got a new constitution in 1964.

Daoud Khan overthrew the king in 1973. The Communists took power in April 1978, and the Soviet Union invaded the country in December 1979 and withdrew in 1989. Civil war followed, the Taliban's rule from 1996, the US-led invasion in 2001 and the Taliban's return in 2021.
Kabul. Wikipedia gives the area as 652,864 km², Wikidata as 652,230 km².
Ahmad Shah Durrani is chosen shah near Kandahar after Nader Shah's death and founds the Durrani Empire.

mapNote.en: Wikipedia gives both 1747 and that the empire was formally founded in 1748. The map shows the empire from 1748, and Cliopatria counts the country's middle as part of Afsharid Iran until 1750.

text.en: On 14 January 1761 Ahmad Shah Durrani's Afghan army defeats the Maratha army at Panipat north of Delhi. The battle is counted as one of the largest and bloodiest of the 18th century.
The Barakzai clan takes Kabul in March 1823, and the Durrani Empire is replaced by the Emirate of Afghanistan.

mapNote.en: Wikidata states that the Durrani Empire ended in 1826. The map shows the Durrani Empire until 1827 and the emirate from 1828.

text.en: Amanullah Khan proclaims himself king on 9 June 1926, seven years after the country became free of British influence in 1919.
While King Zahir Shah is in Italy his cousin Daoud Khan seizes power in a bloodless coup on 17 July 1973, and Afghanistan becomes a republic.
The Taliban, who arose in 1994, drive Rabbani's government out of Kabul in 1996 and proclaim an emirate.

mapNote.en: The map lacks Afghanistan as a whole in 1987–1995, when Cliopatria counts the country's middle as part of the mujahideen. In 1996–2005 the map shows only a small part of the country as Afghanistan and counts the middle as part of the Taliban.

text.en: The United States and Britain begin air strikes on 7 October 2001. The Northern Alliance takes Kabul on 13 November, and by December the Taliban government is overthrown.
The Taliban take Kabul on 15 August 2021 without resistance. President Ashraf Ghani flees, and the Islamic Republic falls.

mapNote.en: The map shows four periods: the Durrani Empire 1748–1827, the emirate 1828–1925, the kingdom 1926–1972 and Afghanistan from 1973. The sources give 1747 for the Durrani Empire and 1823 for the emirate. The map lacks the country in 1987–1995 and shows only a small part of it in 1996–2005, because Cliopatria then counts the country's middle as part of the mujahideen and the Taliban respectively.

summary.en: The Maratha Empire was an empire in western and central India that Shivaji founded in 1674. In the 18th century it grew into a great power that took Delhi, but lost at Panipat in 1761 and fell to the British in 1818.

text.en: Shivaji was crowned chhatrapati on 6 June 1674 and created an independent Maratha state with Raigad as its capital. Later Satara was the king's seat and Pune the peshwa's.
Absolute rule until 1761. After that the empire was governed more as a confederation of princes, with the king as a figurehead. Real power often lay with the peshwa, a kind of prime minister.

The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb waged war against the Marathas in the Deccan in 1680–1707. The Marathas took Delhi in 1760 but lost to the Afghans at Panipat in 1761. Three wars against the British followed, and after the third, 1817–1818, the empire lost its independence.
Raigad (1674–1689), Jinji (1689–1698) and Satara (1700–1818); the peshwa sat in Pune in 1728–1818. At its largest, around 1760, the empire was about 2,500,000 km².
Shivaji is crowned chhatrapati on 6 June 1674 and founds an independent Maratha state with Raigad as its capital.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire only from 1677 and lacks it in 1691–1717.

text.en: Aurangzeb wages war against the Marathas in the Deccan in 1680–1707, which costs the Mughal Empire dearly in both soldiers and money.
Balaji Vishwanath is appointed peshwa on 16 November 1713. Under his son Baji Rao I the empire grows sharply.
The Marathas under Sadashivrao Bhau take Delhi in late July 1760, together with the Jat prince Suraj Mal.
On 14 January 1761 the Marathas lose to Ahmad Shah Durrani's Afghan army at Panipat, and the empire's rapid expansion comes to a halt.
After Peshwa Madhavrao I's death in 1772 Maratha power goes downhill, and the empire becomes more a confederation than an empire.

In the Third Anglo-Maratha War the Marathas lose their independence. The Peshwa is exiled, and the core area with Pune comes under direct British rule. Satara keeps a raja of its own until the British take over in 1848.

mapNote.en: The map shows a small Maratha area up to and including 1845.

The map shows the empire in 1677–1690 and 1718–1845, not from 1674 like the sources. It lacks the empire in 1691–1717 and after 1819 shows only a small area, although the sources say that the empire fell in 1818. Wikipedia's infobox gives the Third Anglo-Maratha War as 1817–1819 and the body text as 1817–1818.

summary.en: Joseon was a kingdom on the Korean Peninsula that was founded in 1392 and ruled by the same royal house for more than 500 years. In 1897 it became the Korean Empire, which Japan annexed in 1910.

text.en: The general Yi Seong-gye staged a coup in the capital Kaegyŏng (present-day Kaesong), overthrew Goryeo's king and became king himself, under the name Taejo, on 5 August 1392. The country was named Joseon in 1393.
Joseon was an absolute monarchy. The Korean Empire was formally also an absolute monarchy but in practice a constitutional monarchy, with Gojong as emperor 1897–1907 and Sunjong 1907–1910.
Japan invaded Korea in 1592 and 1597–1598 without succeeding. The Later Jin dynasty attacked in 1627 and the Qing dynasty in 1636–1637.

Hanseong (present-day Seoul) was the capital from 1394, with an interruption in 1399–1405 when Kaegyŏng was again the capital. Wikipedia gives no area; Wikidata gives about 220,000 km² for Joseon and 220,750 km² for the empire.
Yi Seong-gye overthrows Goryeo's king and becomes King Taejo on 5 August 1392.

mapNote.en: The map shows Joseon only from 1395. Before that Cliopatria shows Goryeo.

text.en: The country is named Joseon in 1393, and the capital is moved from Kaegyŏng to Hanseong. Wikipedia gives 1393 for the move in the introduction but 1394 in the fact box.
King Sejong creates the Korean alphabet, hangul, in 1443. It is promulgated on 9 October 1446.
