Japan's ruler Toyotomi Hideyoshi invades Korea in 1592 and again in 1597. Korea and Ming China drive out the Japanese, but Korea is devastated. Admiral Yi Sun-sin's fleet disrupts the Japanese supply lines across the sea.

mapNote.en: The map shows Joseon with a smaller area in 1595–1599.

text.en: The Later Jin dynasty has attacked in 1627, and in 1636–1637 the Qing dynasty invades Joseon.

mapNote.en: The map shows Joseon with a smaller area in 1636–1639.

text.en: King Gojong proclaims the Korean Empire in October 1897. Wikipedia gives 13 October and Wikidata 12 October.

mapNote.en: The map shows the empire only from 1898.

text.en: By the Eulsa Treaty of 17 November 1905 the empire becomes a protectorate under Japan.
Japan annexes Korea on 29 August 1910, and the empire ceases to exist.

mapNote.en: The map shows Joseon 1395–1897 and the empire 1898–1910. The sources give 1392 for Joseon's founding and October 1897 for the empire. The area on the map is smaller in 1595–1599 and 1636–1639.

summary.en: North Korea, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, is a communist state in the northern part of the Korean Peninsula. It was formed on 9 September 1948 and has since been ruled by Kim Il Sung, his son and his grandson.

text.en: After Japan's surrender in 1945 Korea was divided into two zones along the 38th parallel. The Soviet Union ruled north of the border from 24 August 1945, and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea was formed on 9 September 1948.
A communist unitary state with juche as the state ideology. The present constitution dates from 27 December 1972.
Kim Il Sung was the country's first leader. After his death in 1994 his son Kim Jong Il took over, and when Kim Jong Il died on 17 December 2011 he was succeeded by his son Kim Jong Un.
Pyongyang. The area is about 120,540 km².
The Democratic People's Republic of Korea is formed on 9 September 1948 north of the 38th parallel.
North Korean forces cross the 38th parallel on 25 June 1950, and the Korean War begins.
The armistice is signed at Panmunjom on 27 July 1953. It creates the demilitarised zone between North and South Korea, but no peace treaty is ever concluded.

mapNote.en: The map shows North Korea with a somewhat smaller area from 1953.

text.en: The present constitution is adopted on 27 December 1972.
North Korea joins the UN in 1991, at the same time as South Korea.

title.en: Kim Jong Il and the famine

text.en: Kim Il Sung dies in 1994, and his son Kim Jong Il takes over. The famine in the mid-1990s costs an estimated 240,000–420,000 people their lives.
North Korea announces in 2006 that the country has carried out its first nuclear test.
Kim Jong Il dies on 17 December 2011, and his son Kim Jong Un becomes the country's leader.

mapNote.en: The map shows North Korea from 1948, like the sources. Before that Cliopatria counts the area as part of the Japanese Empire.

summary.en: South Korea, the Republic of Korea, lies in the southern part of the Korean Peninsula and was formed on 15 August 1948. The country went from poverty and dictatorship to a strong economy and, after 1987, democracy.

text.en: After Japan's surrender in 1945 Korea was divided along the 38th parallel, and the United States ruled south of the border from 8 September 1945. The Republic of Korea was formed on 15 August 1948.
A presidential republic. The present constitution dates from 29 October 1987, after the democracy movement the same year.
During the period called the “Miracle on the Han River” the economy grew by an average of 10 per cent a year between 1962 and 1994.
Seoul. The area is 100,472 km².
The Republic of Korea is formed on 15 August 1948 south of the 38th parallel. The same year the country's first direct election is held.

mapNote.en: Cliopatria also places an entry for the United States over the country's middle in 1948–1966.

text.en: North Korea attacks on 25 June 1950 and takes Seoul. The UN forces hold the Pusan Perimeter and turn the war with the landing at Inchon on 15 September.
The fighting ends with the armistice on 27 July 1953. South Korea does not sign, and no peace treaty is ever concluded.
A student uprising, the April Revolution, forces the autocratic president Syngman Rhee to resign in 1960.
General Park Chung Hee takes power in a military coup on 16 May 1961.
Special forces crush the democracy movement in Gwangju on 18–27 May 1980. Probably between 500 and 2,000 civilians are killed.
The June movement of 1987 ends the authoritarian rule, and a new constitution is adopted on 29 October 1987.
Seoul hosts the Summer Olympics in 1988.

mapNote.en: The map shows South Korea from 1948, like the sources. Before that Cliopatria counts the area as part of the Japanese Empire. Cliopatria also places an entry for the United States over the same area in 1948–1966.

summary.en: Ho Chi Minh proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam on 2 September 1945. After the Geneva Accords in 1954 it ruled the northern part of the country, North Vietnam, and after the victory in the Vietnam War the country was united on 2 July 1976 as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

text.en: The Viet Minh took power in the August Revolution of 1945, and Ho Chi Minh proclaimed independence on 2 September 1945. The Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954 divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel.
North Vietnam was a communist unitary state with a constitution on the Soviet model. Today's Vietnam is also a communist unitary state.
The Communist Party began market reforms in 1986 under the name Đổi Mới. Vietnam became a member of the WTO on 11 January 2007.
Hanoi. North Vietnam had an area of 157,880 km² and today's Vietnam has 331,345 km².
Ho Chi Minh proclaims the Democratic Republic of Vietnam on 2 September 1945, after the August Revolution and Japan's surrender.

mapNote.en: The map does not show the state before 1956. Cliopatria counts the country in 1946 as part of French Indochina.

text.en: The war against France begins on 19 December 1946.

The Viet Minh defeat the French at Điện Biên Phủ in 1954. The Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954 divide Vietnam at the 17th parallel, and the elections on a united country that were to be held in 1956 never take place.
After the Gulf of Tonkin incident in August 1964 the US Congress gives President Johnson authority to deploy American forces. The United States takes part with its own combat troops in 1965–1973.
Ho Chi Minh dies on 2 September 1969.
North Vietnam's army and the NLF take Saigon on 30 April 1975, and the war is over.

mapNote.en: The map shows North Vietnam with a larger area in 1973–1975.

text.en: North and South are formally united on 2 July 1976 as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
The Communist Party's Sixth Congress introduces the Đổi Mới market reforms in 1986.

mapNote.en: The map shows North Vietnam 1956–1975 and the united Vietnam from 1976. The sources give 1945 for the state's founding and 1954 for the partition. Cliopatria also places an entry for the United States over southern Vietnam in 1967–2005.

summary.en: South Vietnam, the Republic of Vietnam, was a state in southern Vietnam with Saigon as its capital. The republic was proclaimed on 26 October 1955 and ceased to exist when Saigon fell on 30 April 1975.

text.en: The State of Vietnam was formed in 1949. After a referendum in 1955, marked by extensive electoral fraud, Bảo Đại was deposed and Ngô Đình Diệm proclaimed the republic on 26 October 1955.
A presidential republic 1955–1963, a military junta 1963–1967 and a semi-presidential republic 1967–1975. Presidents were Ngô Đình Diệm 1955–1963, Nguyễn Văn Thiệu 1967–1975 and Dương Văn Minh 1975.
North Vietnam supported the insurgency in the south, and the United States supported South Vietnam. American combat troops took part in 1965–1973.
Saigon (today Ho Chi Minh City). The area was 173,809 km².
Ngô Đình Diệm proclaims the Republic of Vietnam on 26 October 1955, after a referendum with extensive electoral fraud.

mapNote.en: The map shows South Vietnam only from 1956.

text.en: Diệm is killed in 1963 in a military coup led by General Dương Văn Minh and supported by the CIA.
American marines and army soldiers are deployed in 1965. In November the first major battle between the American and North Vietnamese armies takes place at Ia Drang.
North Vietnam's army and the NLF attack more than 100 cities in South Vietnam on 30–31 January 1968, among them Saigon. The attacks are beaten back.

mapNote.en: The map lacks South Vietnam in 1967–1972, when Cliopatria instead shows the United States over the area.

text.en: A ceasefire is concluded in Paris in January 1973, but the fighting soon begins again.
President Dương Văn Minh surrenders on 30 April 1975, and South Vietnam ceases to exist.

mapNote.en: The map shows South Vietnam 1956–1966 and 1973–1975 but lacks the country in 1967–1972, when Cliopatria instead shows the United States over the area (the United States remains over southern Vietnam until 2005). The republic was proclaimed in October 1955.

summary.en: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom was a theocratic monarchy in southern and eastern China that wanted to overthrow the Qing dynasty. It was founded in 1851 by Hong Xiuquan, had Nanjing as its capital from 1853 and fell in 1864.

text.en: The rebellion began in Guangxi in 1850, and on 11 January 1851 Hong Xiuquan proclaimed himself “Heavenly King” of a new dynasty.
Hong Xiuquan claimed to be Jesus's younger brother, and the movement mixed Protestant Christianity with Chinese religion. The kingdom was a theocratic absolute monarchy.
The kingdom abolished private ownership of land, so that the state owned and distributed all land, and banned foot binding.
The Taiping Rebellion is counted as the deadliest civil war in history. Most estimates are 20–30 million dead.
Tianjing, “the Heavenly Capital”, that is Nanjing.
Hong Xiuquan proclaims the uprising at Jintian and founds the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom on 11 January 1851.

mapNote.en: The map shows the kingdom only from 1853.

text.en: The Taiping army conquers Nanjing on 19 March 1853 and makes the city its capital, Tianjing. An army sets out the same year against Beijing but is annihilated by 1855.
The Taiping leaders fight each other in the capital from 2 September 1856. Yang Xiuqing and more than 27,000 others are killed, and the movement is weakened.
Zeng Guofan's army takes Anqing on 5 September 1861 and opens the way to Nanjing. The Taipings' attack on Shanghai in 1861–1862 is beaten back.

mapNote.en: The map shows the kingdom at its largest in 1861, about 348,000 km².

text.en: Hong Xiuquan dies on 1 June 1864, and the Qing army takes Nanjing on 19 July. His son and successor Hong Tianguifu is captured on 25 October 1864. Scattered Taiping forces continue to resist, and the last rebel army is annihilated in August 1871.

mapNote.en: The map shows the kingdom 1853–1864. The sources state that it was founded in January 1851; Nanjing was taken in 1853.

summary.en: Nigeria is a federal republic in West Africa and Africa's most populous country, with Abuja as its capital. The country became independent from Britain on 1 October 1960.

text.en: The country took its present form in 1914, when the British merged the protectorates of Southern and Northern Nigeria. It became independent as a federal state on 1 October 1960.
Emeka Ojukwu proclaimed south-eastern Nigeria the independent state of Biafra in 1967. The war began on 6 July 1967 and ended in January 1970, after a long blockade of Biafra.

After the civil war several military dictatorships followed, with a short democratic period in 1979–1983. Since 1999 the country has been a stable democracy, when the military rule under Abubakar handed over power to the elected president Olusegun Obasanjo.

Over 250 ethnic groups with 500 languages. The largest are the Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo, together over 60 per cent. The official language is English, and the country is roughly half Muslim and half Christian.

summary.en: The Democratic Republic of the Congo, often called Congo-Kinshasa, is a country in Central Africa around the Congo Basin, with Kinshasa as its capital. It became independent from Belgium on 30 June 1960.

text.en: Belgium's King Leopold II received the right to the area in 1885 and called it the Congo Free State. After international protests against the abuses he handed it over in 1908, and it became a Belgian colony. Independence came on 30 June 1960, under the name Republic of the Congo.

Immediately after independence came secessions and the murder of Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba. Mobutu Sese Seko took power in 1965 and renamed the country Zaire in 1971. He was overthrown in 1997 by Laurent-Désiré Kabila, who gave the country its name back.
The First Congo War of 1996–1997 followed the flow of refugees from the civil war in Rwanda. The Second Congo War of 1998–2003 claimed, according to estimates, several million lives.
Kinshasa. French is the official language; there are over 200 indigenous languages, and Lingala is the most widely spoken.

summary.en: Rwanda is a small, densely populated country in East Africa's lake region, with Kigali as its capital. It became independent on 1 July 1962.

text.en: The Kingdom of Rwanda emerged in the 15th century and dominated the area from the middle of the 18th century. Germany made it part of German East Africa in 1897, and Belgium took over in 1916. The country was separated from Burundi and became independent on 1 July 1962.

The Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF) began a civil war in 1990. When President Habyarimana's aircraft was shot down on 6 April 1994 the genocide began: in about 100 days between 500,000 and 1,000,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed. The RPF took control of the country in mid-July.
Since 1994 the country has in practice been ruled as a one-party state by the RPF, with Paul Kagame as president since 2000.
Kigali. The area is 26,338 km².

summary.en: Uganda is a country in East Africa's lake region, named after the Kingdom of Buganda, with Kampala as its capital. It became independent from Britain on 9 October 1962.

text.en: The British established the Uganda Protectorate in 1894. The country became independent on 9 October 1962, with Milton Obote as its first prime minister.

The Mengo Crisis of 1966 led to conflict with the Kingdom of Buganda and to the country becoming a presidential republic. Idi Amin overthrew Obote in a military coup in 1971 and ruled as a brutal dictator until he was overthrown in 1979 in the war between Uganda and Tanzania.
After the disputed election in 1980 a six-year guerrilla war followed, which Yoweri Museveni's National Resistance Movement won in 1986. Museveni has been president ever since.
Kampala. Official languages are English and Swahili.
Uganda becomes independent on 9 October 1962.

summary.en: The Zulu Kingdom was a kingdom in southern Africa, along the Indian Ocean coast between the Tugela and Pongola rivers, in present-day KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa. Shaka built it up in the 1810s, and the British conquered it in 1879.

text.en: The kingdom emerged during the mfecane, a time of unrest and state formation in southern Africa. Shaka became Zulu king and after Dingiswayo's death around 1816 took the leadership of the whole Mthethwa confederation. He built a standing army, the amabutho, and expanded the kingdom through war and diplomacy.

Shaka was murdered in 1828 by his half-brothers and succeeded by Dingane. Later kings included Cetshwayo. A civil war in the 1850s ended with the Battle of Ndondakusuka in 1856 between the brothers Cetshwayo and Mbuyazi.

The British invaded Zululand in 1879. The Zulus won at Isandlwana in January, but the British defeated them at Ulundi in July, and Cetshwayo was captured on 28 August. The kingdom was divided among eleven Zulu chiefs and two others, and the British annexed Zululand in 1887. The area became part of Natal and later South Africa.

summary.en: Australia is a federal state and constitutional monarchy comprising the Australian continent, with Canberra as its capital. The colonies joined together in the Commonwealth of Australia in 1901.

text.en: The ancestors of the Aboriginal people arrived 50,000–65,000 years ago. British colonisation began in 1788 with the penal colony of New South Wales. The six colonies joined together in 1901 and formed the Commonwealth of Australia.

At the time of British settlement the Aboriginal people spoke more than 250 languages. After the referendum in 1967 the federal government was allowed to legislate for Aboriginal people, and they were counted fully in the census.
Self-government from Britain grew step by step, with the Statute of Westminster, which Australia adopted in 1942, and finally the Australia Act 1986.
Canberra. The largest cities are Sydney and Melbourne.
The British found the penal colony of New South Wales.

summary.en: New Zealand is an island nation in the south-western Pacific with Wellington as its capital. Polynesians settled the islands between about 1280 and 1350, and the country became fully independent from Britain in 1947.

text.en: The islands were the last large habitable land that humans settled. Polynesians came between about 1280 and 1350 and developed Māori culture. Abel Tasman was the first European to see the islands, in 1642, and James Cook the first to go ashore and chart them, in 1769.

Britain and Māori chiefs signed the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840, and the colony of New Zealand was formed in 1841. In the New Zealand Wars that followed the Māori lost large areas of land through confiscations.
New Zealand became a dominion in 1907 and gained full independence in law in 1947, with the monarch remaining as head of state.
In 1893 New Zealand was the first country in the world to give all women the right to vote.

summary.en: Papua New Guinea comprises the eastern half of New Guinea and hundreds of islands, with Port Moresby as its capital. It became independent from Australia on 16 September 1975 and is the world's most linguistically diverse country.

text.en: Eastern New Guinea was divided in 1884 between German New Guinea in the north and British New Guinea in the south, which Australia took over in 1902. Australia occupied the German part during the First World War, and the two territories were united in 1949. Independence came on 16 September 1975.
A new uprising on Bougainville began in 1988, against both the island's and the country's government.
There are 840 known languages. English and Tok Pisin serve as common languages. Most people live in rural areas.
Port Moresby. The area is 462,840 km².

summary.en: Canada is a federal state and constitutional monarchy in North America, the world's second largest country by area, with Ottawa as its capital. The country was formed as a dominion in 1867 and became independent from Britain step by step.

text.en: Indigenous peoples have lived in the area for thousands of years. From the 16th century the British and French explored and settled the Atlantic coast, and France ceded almost all its colonies in North America in 1763. Three British colonies joined together in 1867 and formed the Dominion of Canada, with four provinces.

New provinces and territories were added, which pushed aside the Indigenous population. The Statute of Westminster in 1931 gave the country greater independence, and the Canada Act 1982 cut the last legal ties to the British Parliament.
A parliamentary democracy with the monarch as formal head of state. The federation is officially bilingual, with English and French.
Ottawa. The largest metropolitan areas are Toronto, Montréal and Vancouver.

summary.en: Chile is a republic along South America's west coast, between the Andes and the Pacific, with Santiago as its capital. The country declared independence from Spain in 1818.

text.en: Spain conquered the area in the middle of the 16th century but never defeated the Mapuche people in the south. Chile declared independence in 1818 and became a relatively stable authoritarian republic in the 1830s.
During the 19th century the country grew. The Mapuche resistance was broken in the 1880s, and in the War of the Pacific against Peru and Bolivia Chile gained its present northern area.

The coup on 11 September 1973, with support from the United States, overthrew Salvador Allende's elected left-wing government. Augusto Pinochet's military dictatorship lasted sixteen and a half years, with over 3,000 dead and disappeared, and ended in 1990 after a referendum in 1988.
Santiago. The area is 756,102 km².

summary.en: Peru is a republic in western South America with Lima as its capital. Here lay Caral–Supe, the Americas' earliest civilisation, and the Inca Empire. The country proclaimed its independence from Spain in 1821 and completed it in 1824.

text.en: Spain conquered the area in the 16th century, and the Viceroyalty of Peru was governed from Lima. Peru proclaimed its independence in 1821, and after the campaigns under O'Higgins, San Martín and Bolívar and the decisive Battle of Ayacucho it was completed in 1824.

A period of relative stability thanks to guano exports ended with the War of the Pacific in 1879–1884. The sources differ about the end year: Wikipedia's article on Chile gives 1879–1883, the article on Peru 1879–1884.

The country was marked by political and social unrest, among other things the conflict between the state and guerrilla groups such as the Shining Path. Alberto Fujimori ruled authoritarianly in the 1990s.

summary.en: Bolivia is a landlocked country in central South America. The government sits in La Paz, while Sucre is the capital according to the constitution. The republic, named after Simón Bolívar, was proclaimed on 6 August 1825.

text.en: The area belonged to Tiwanaku, which fell around the year 1000, and its western part came under the Inca Empire in the 1440s. Under Spain it was governed by the Audiencia of Charcas, and the silver of Potosí carried large parts of the Spanish Empire. After a failed uprising in Sucre in 1809 sixteen years of war followed, until the republic was proclaimed on 6 August 1825.
Bolivia lost its coast to Chile from 1879, Acre to Brazil in 1899–1903 and most of the Gran Chaco to Paraguay in the Chaco War of 1932–1935.
The national revolution of 1952 gave universal suffrage, nationalised the tin mines and carried out a limited land reform. The last non-elected military ruler left power in 1982.

summary.en: Colombia is a republic in north-western South America with Bogotá as its capital. The country declared independence in 1810 and has changed its name and form of government several times; the present name and centralised republic date from 1886.

text.en: The Spaniards landed in La Guajira in 1499 and by the middle of the 16th century had colonised most of the area as New Granada. Independence was declared in 1810, and the area became the United Provinces of New Granada. After a Spanish reconquest independence was secured, and Gran Colombia was formed in 1819.
After Gran Colombia came the Granadine Confederation (1858), the United States of Colombia (1863) and from 1886 the Republic of Colombia, a centralised republic.
With support from the United States and France, Panama broke away in 1903, and Colombia got its present borders.
Since the 1960s the country has been affected by an armed conflict and political violence, which escalated in the 1990s. Since 2000 security has improved.
Independence is declared, and the United Provinces of New Granada are formed.

summary.en: Venezuela is a federal republic on South America's north coast with Caracas as its capital. The country declared independence from Spain in 1811 and became a state of its own in 1830.

text.en: Spain colonised the area from 1522, against the resistance of Indigenous peoples. Venezuela was in 1811 one of the first Spanish American areas to declare independence, and it was then part of Gran Colombia. The country became a fully independent state in 1830.

During the 19th century the country was dominated by regional military dictators, well into the 20th century. From 1958 it had democratic governments, as an exception in a region of military dictatorships.

Economic shocks in the 1980s and 1990s led to the Caracazo riots in 1989 and two coup attempts in 1992. Hugo Chávez was elected in 1998, and a new constitution was written in 1999. The elections of 2013, 2018 and 2024 were disputed.
Caracas. The area is 912,050 km².

summary.en: Ecuador is a republic in north-western South America with Quito as its capital, and also comprises the Galápagos Islands. The country became independent in 1820 as part of Gran Colombia and a state of its own on 13 May 1830.

text.en: The Indigenous peoples of the area became part of the Inca Empire in the 15th century, and Spain colonised it in the 16th century. Ecuador became independent in 1820 as part of Gran Colombia and broke away on 13 May 1830. The first president was General Juan José Flores.
The constitution of 2008 was the first in the world to give nature rights that can be enforced in court.
Most are mestizos. Spanish is the official language, and 13 indigenous languages are recognised, among them Quechua and Shuar.

summary.en: Haiti lies on the western part of the island of Hispaniola, with Port-au-Prince as its capital. The Haitian Revolution of 1791–1804 made the country the only state in history created through a slave uprising.

text.en: The island was inhabited by the Taíno people. Columbus founded La Navidad in 1492, and the island belonged to Spain until the western part was ceded to France in 1697 and became the plantation colony of Saint-Domingue. The leaders of the revolution proclaimed independence on 1 January 1804, and Dessalines became emperor.

The new state was at first an empire, was then divided in two and reunited in 1820. Faustin Soulouque founded a second empire before the republic returned in 1859. The country suffered from political unrest, isolation and a crippling debt to France.

The United States occupied Haiti in 1915–1934, and the Duvalier family ruled as dictators in 1957–1986. An earthquake and a cholera outbreak struck the country in the 2010s. The presidency has been vacant since the murder of Jovenel Moïse in July 2021.

summary.en: Ukraine is a republic in Eastern Europe with Kyiv as its capital. The country became independent in 1991, when the Soviet Union was dissolved. In 2014 the war with Russia began.

text.en: The Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian SSR adopted the declaration of independence on 24 August 1991. In a referendum on 1 December 1991 over 90 per cent voted for independence. Poland and Canada were the first to recognise the country, on 2 December, and the Soviet Union was dissolved on 26 December 1991.
A semi-presidential republic.

The Orange Revolution of 2004–2005 followed a presidential election that according to critics was full of fraud. The revolution in February 2014, at the end of the Euromaidan protests, led to parliament removing President Viktor Yanukovych.

After the revolution of 2014 Russia occupied and annexed the Crimean Peninsula, and in Donbas a war began between Ukraine and separatists with Russian support. On 24 February 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Kyiv. The area is 603,628 km² according to Wikipedia and 603,550 km² according to Wikidata.

The Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian SSR declares Ukraine independent on 24 August 1991, with 346 votes to 1. In the referendum on 1 December over 90 per cent vote yes, and 84 per cent of those entitled to vote take part.

mapNote.en: The map shows Ukraine only from 1992. In 1991 Cliopatria counts the area as part of the Soviet Union.

text.en: After the second round of the presidential election on 21 November 2004 between Viktor Yushchenko and Viktor Yanukovych, people protest against electoral fraud. The Supreme Court orders a rerun, which is held on 26 December, and Yushchenko wins with about 52 per cent of the votes.

The Euromaidan protests begin in November 2013, when President Yanukovych suddenly decides not to sign the association agreement with the EU. In February 2014 many demonstrators are killed by government forces in Kyiv, and on 22 February parliament votes to remove Yanukovych.

On 27 February 2014 Russian special forces without insignia begin to take control of key places in Crimea. After a referendum that Wikipedia calls illegitimate, Russia incorporates the peninsula on 18 March 2014. The UN General Assembly confirms Ukraine's borders in Resolution 68/262, and Ukraine and many other countries regard the annexation as a violation of international law.

mapNote.en: The border is disputed. Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, but Sweden does not recognise the annexation and counts Crimea and Sevastopol as part of Ukraine. The map follows Sweden's official position according to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD) (checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria also counts Crimea as part of Russia in 2014–2023 and only as part of Russia in 2024.

text.en: In April 2014 paramilitary groups with Russian support begin an uprising in eastern Ukraine, and Ukraine's army counterattacks. Russia's military takes part in secret. A new ceasefire, Minsk II, is concluded on 12 February 2015. About 14,000 people are killed before the war escalates in 2022 into the full-scale invasion.

On 24 February 2022 Russia attacks Ukraine, a sharp escalation of the war that began in 2014. Russian forces try to take Kyiv from the north, but by 2 April Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast are again under Ukrainian control.

On 30 September 2022 Russia unilaterally declares that it is annexing the Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts, after referendums organised by the Russian occupation authorities. Russia does not control any of the provinces completely. The annexation is not recognised by the rest of the world, except by North Korea, and 143 of the UN's member states condemn it as illegal.

mapNote.en: The map counts the areas that Russia has occupied since 2022 as part of Ukraine, and does not show the front line.

The map shows Ukraine from 1992; according to the sources the country became independent on 24 August 1991, and the Soviet Union was dissolved on 26 December 1991. Crimea and Sevastopol are shown as part of Ukraine throughout, also after Russia's annexation in 2014, because in disputed borders the map follows Sweden's official position according to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD) (checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria also counts Crimea as part of Russia in 2014–2023 and only as part of Russia in 2024. The areas that Russia has occupied since 2022 are shown as part of Ukraine, in accordance with both Cliopatria and Sweden's position. The map ends in 2024 and says nothing about the situation after that.

summary.en: The Russian Federation, or Russia, emerged from the Russian SFSR when the Soviet Union was dissolved in 1991, and is counted as the Soviet Union's successor state. The capital is Moscow.

text.en: The Russian SFSR declared itself sovereign on 12 June 1990. On 8 December 1991 the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed the Belovezha Accords, which stated that the Soviet Union no longer existed. The Soviet Union was formally dissolved on 26 December 1991. Wikidata gives 25 December 1991 as the beginning of the Russian Federation.

A federal, semi-presidential republic. The constitution dates from 12 December 1993. Since the turn of the century Vladimir Putin has dominated politics, and according to Wikipedia the country has become increasingly authoritarian under his leadership.

Russia fought two wars in Chechnya, in 1994–1996 and from 1999, and a war against Georgia in 2008. In 2014 Russia annexed Crimea, which is not recognised internationally, and since then the country has been at war against Ukraine. After the invasion of 2022 Russia declared four more Ukrainian provinces annexed.
Moscow. The area within the internationally recognised borders is 17,098,246 km² according to Wikipedia; Wikidata gives 17,075,400 km².

The leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus sign the Belovezha Accords on 8 December 1991. Mikhail Gorbachev resigns on 25 December and hands over his powers, also the control of nuclear weapons, to Boris Yeltsin. The next day the Soviet Union is formally dissolved, and Russia becomes its recognised successor state.

mapNote.en: The map shows the Russian Federation only from 1992. In 1991 Cliopatria counts the area as part of the Soviet Union.

text.en: On 21 September 1993 President Yeltsin dissolves parliament, in violation of the constitution then in force. On 4 October the army storms the parliament building in Moscow; according to the Russian government's figures 147 people are killed. A new constitution is adopted on 12 December 1993.

Russian troops enter Chechnya on 11 December 1994. The war ends on 31 August 1996 with the Khasavyurt Accord, and the Russian forces withdraw. Between 30,000 and 100,000 Chechen civilians are estimated to have been killed.

title.en: The Second Chechen War and Putin

text.en: In August 1999 Islamists from Chechnya push into Dagestan, and the war in Chechnya begins anew. Yeltsin resigns on 31 December 1999, and Prime Minister Vladimir Putin becomes acting president; he is elected in March 2000. The government's operation in Chechnya is officially ended in April 2009.

Russian special forces without insignia begin to take control of Crimea on 27 February 2014, and on 18 March Russia incorporates the peninsula into Russia. The annexation is not recognised internationally, and the same spring the war in Donbas begins.

mapNote.en: The border is disputed. Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, but Sweden does not recognise the annexation and counts Crimea and Sevastopol as part of Ukraine. The map follows Sweden's official position according to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD) (checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria counts Crimea as part of Russia from 2014.

text.en: On 24 February 2022 Russia attacks Ukraine, a sharp escalation of the war that began in 2014. On 30 September 2022 Russia declares four Ukrainian provinces annexed, although it does not control any of them completely. The annexation is not recognised by the rest of the world, except by North Korea.

mapNote.en: The map does not count the areas in Ukraine that Russia has occupied since 2022 as part of Russia.

The map shows the Russian Federation from 1992; according to the sources the Soviet Union was dissolved in December 1991. Crimea and Sevastopol are not counted as part of Russia, because in disputed borders the map follows Sweden's official position according to the Swedish Foreign Ministry (UD): Sweden does not recognise the annexation of 2014 (checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria counts Crimea as part of Russia in 2014–2024. The areas in Ukraine that Russia has occupied since 2022 are not counted as part of Russia either. The map ends in 2024 and says nothing about the situation after that.

The map shows the Republic of China 1912–1949 and the People's Republic of China from 1950. Cliopatria lacks the Republic of China in 1916–1929. After 1949 Taiwan is shown as an area of its own (see Taiwan). The border in Kashmir is disputed: Cliopatria counts the north-eastern part of Kashmir as part of China, and the map shows who controls the areas, not whom they belong to. Sweden has no stated position on Kashmir that we have found (UD, checked 2026-11-06).

Taiwan's status is disputed. The map shows Taiwan as an area of its own with Cliopatria's border (the Republic of China after 1949) and under the name Taiwan, which the government uses. Sweden has no diplomatic relations with Taiwan but a trade office in Taipei, and we have not found any stated Swedish position on Taiwan's status (UD, checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria shows a smaller area in 2024 than in 1950–2023.

Timor-Leste is not counted as part of Indonesia. Indonesia occupied the territory in 1975, but Sweden never recognised the occupation, and the UN never recognised Indonesia's integration of the territory either (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs and UN, checked 2026-11-06). The border is disputed, and the map follows Sweden's official position. Cliopatria counts Timor-Leste as part of Indonesia in 1976–2005.

The map shows Morocco 1670–1911 and from 1956; in between Cliopatria counts the country as part of the French colonial empire. Western Sahara's status is disputed and is to be decided in a UN-led process. Sweden supports the UN process and sees Morocco's autonomy plan as a credible basis for negotiations, but has not stated whom the area belongs to (UD, checked 2026-11-06). The map therefore does not count Western Sahara as part of Morocco, and neither does Cliopatria.

Kosovo is not part of Serbia on the map, nor in Cliopatria. Kosovo is shown as a separate state from the declaration of independence in 2008, by decision of Historia-globen; Sweden has had diplomatic relations with Kosovo since then (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). In the years before 2008 Kosovo is shown without a state, because the area was administered by the UN and its status had not been settled.

The border is disputed. Nagorno-Karabakh and surrounding areas, which Cliopatria counts as part of Armenia, are shown without a state up to and including 2022 and as part of Azerbaijan from 2023, because the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs writes that Azerbaijan re-established its control over Nagorno-Karabakh in the autumn of 2023 (checked 2026-11-06). The border of the area comes from Natural Earth.

The border is disputed. Cliopatria counts Nagorno-Karabakh and surrounding areas as part of Armenia. The map does not show them as Armenia: up to and including 2022 they are shown without a state, as disputed, and from 2023 as part of Azerbaijan, because the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs writes that Azerbaijan then re-established its control over Nagorno-Karabakh (checked 2026-11-06). The area is the part of Cliopatria's Armenia that lies within Azerbaijan's border in Natural Earth.

The border is disputed. Abkhazia and South Ossetia are drawn as part of Georgia, because for disputed borders the map follows Sweden's official position: Sweden supports Georgia's territorial integrity (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). According to Natural Earth, the areas are self-governing. The map shows Georgia in 1918–1921 and from 1992, as Cliopatria does.

text.en: The white cross on red. The federal coat of arms was defined in 1815, and from 1840 the flag is shown, which was first the banner of the cantonal troops under federal command. The sources differ on the year of the flag: 1840 in the infobox and 1841 in the text on Wikipedia. The proportions of the cross have been fixed since 1889. Before 1815 no symbol is shown.

mapNote.en: The border is disputed. Transnistria is drawn as part of Moldova, by decision of Historia-globen. The Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs describes Transnistria as a region of Moldova but has no stated position on the area's status that we have found (checked 2026-11-06). According to Natural Earth, the area is self-governing. Cliopatria counts Transnistria as part of Russia, as an occupied territory.

Kosovo is shown as a separate state from the declaration of independence in 2008, by decision of Historia-globen. Sweden has had diplomatic relations with Kosovo since then (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). In 2000–2007 the area is shown without a state: Kosovo was administered by the UN and its status had not been settled. Sweden concluded an agreement with the UN administration (UNMIK, SÖ 2005:29), and in 2007 negotiations on Kosovo's future status were under way (Swedish government communication 2007/08:82). Cliopatria shows Kosovo as a separate state from as early as 2000.

The island is divided. From 1976 the whole island is drawn as Cyprus, by decision of Historia-globen. Since 1974 the island has been divided by a UN-controlled buffer zone, and the area north of the zone is not controlled by the government of the Republic of Cyprus. Sweden does not recognise the independence of Northern Cyprus, in accordance with UN Security Council resolution 541 of 1983 (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, checked 2026-11-06). Cliopatria shows Northern Cyprus as a separate state from 1976.

Timor-Leste is shown as a separate state from independence on 20 May 2002 (UN). Indonesia occupied the territory in 1975. Sweden never recognised the occupation, and the UN never recognised Indonesia's integration of the territory either (Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs and UN, checked 2026-11-06). The map follows Sweden's official position: in 1976–2001 the territory is not counted as part of Indonesia and is shown without a state. The UN administered the territory from October 1999 until independence. The sources differ: Cliopatria counts Timor-Leste as part of Indonesia until 2005 and as a separate state from 2006, and Wikidata gives 28 November 1975 as its start date.

text.en: The golden fleurs-de-lis on blue, the arms of the kings 1211–1792. At first the lilies were scattered over the shield with no fixed number, and in 1376 Charles V reduced them to three. Before 1211 no symbol is shown.

The black banner, the colour of the Abbasids. According to the historian Tayeb El-Hibri, an envoy of Ali ibn Yusuf came to Baghdad in 1104 and declared allegiance to the Abbasids. Some authors instead read the black as the fight against unbelief. The same colour is the Abbasids' sign on the map. The banner is shown 1104–1147, when the Almoravids fell to the Almohads according to the source; the map data continues until 1205.

The white banner. Most historical sources say that the Almohads were known for white banners, already under the movement's founder Ibn Tumart. Whether the banners had particular motifs or inscriptions is not certain, so only the colour is shown here. The banner is shown until 1269, when the caliphate ended according to the source; the map data continues until 1343.
The white eagle on red. The image is based on a modern reconstruction of the arms on the reverse of Przemysł II's majestic seal from 1295 and is simplified here. Before 1295 no symbol is shown.
